payload.body:
Closing in favor of an egress-jail-based cost recorder. Vargas pointed out (correctly) that synthesizing `usage` events from `usage_progress` only works for the Vellum daemon harness — every other benchmark harness needs its own translation layer.

The egress jail already sees every LLM HTTP request/response on the way out, regardless of which provider client (or which evals harness) made the call. Recording usage/cost there means a single source of truth across all harnesses with no per-harness shim.

Will draft the spec for the egress-jail-based recorder before writing code so we agree on the shape first.

payload.author: vellum-apollo-bot
payload.body:
Closing — this was the wrong abstraction layer.

The right place to capture LLM usage is the egress jail (`evals/src/lib/egress/`), which is already wired into the runner generically (`agent.readUsageRecords?.()` at `run-once.ts:325`) and is already invoked on every vellum-* run via `applyDockerEgressJail` in the vellum adapter. Doing it at the jail boundary captures real wire-level usage for **every** harness (vellum, hermes, future adapters) instead of needing per-adapter shape translation.

The Tier B run's `egress-usage.ndjson` was created but empty — that's the actual bug to chase. Followup: investigate why the mitmproxy sidecar did not intercept the assistant container's Anthropic calls on the AWS sandbox.

payload.author: siddseethepalli
payload.body:
<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Memory v3 — Self-Maintaining Structure</summary>

# Memory v3 — Self-Maintaining Structure

## Overview

Make the memory-v3 topic tree **self-maintaining** so it stays coherent as the
corpus grows and reorganizes over weeks/months, without a human babysitting a
batch script. The maintainer (the assistant) keeps her own structure current as
a natural extension of how she already consolidates memory; deterministic
plumbing keeps referential integrity; a green-suppressed health report surfaces
the cases automation can't resolve.

Four capabilities, mirroring how v2 consolidation already works (an assistant
turn for judgment + a mechanical follow-up for indexing):

1. **Assignment stays current** — page→leaf assignment lives in page frontmatter
   (`leaves:`), exactly like v2's `edges:`. The maintainer sets it as she files a
   page; a post-consolidation classifier **unions in** anything she missed; the
   needle index rebuilds. Drift becomes structurally hard.
2. **Health report** — at the consolidation trigger, a flag-gated block reports
   coverage gaps, pipeline failures, and judgment-only candidates (new leaves,
   stale labels). Shown only when something is actionable.
3. **Tree gardening** — the maintainer can restructure the tree (add / rename /
   move / split / merge / delete leaves). A deterministic reconciler keeps all
   references intact, re-homes pages so none are orphaned, and snapshots for
   rollback. Stable leaf `id`s make reorg cheap and safe to repeat.
4. **Core editing** — the maintainer owns the always-on `core.json` set, with
   validation and an always-on page-count/cost preview.

## Design rationale (the "why")

- **Why frontmatter, not `assignments.json`:** v2 already stores structural links
  (`edges:`) in page frontmatter as the single source of truth — no side table.
  Mirroring that makes assignment *born with the page and maintained with it*, so
  it can't silently drift. `assignments.json` becomes a derived/fallback export,
  not the source.
- **Why union (maintainer ∪ classifier):** the maintainer read the source
  material and has context a summary-only classifier lacks (cross-domain links,
  nuance); the classifier systematically sweeps all leaves and catches the
  obvious homes she skips mid-consolidation. Unioning their picks yields strictly
  higher recall than either alone, consistent with the multi-home design. Cost:
  multi-home creeps from ~3.2 toward ~4–5 leaves/page — acceptable; L2 + the
  working-set cap absorb it.
- **Why a health report even with auto-classify:** automation can fail silently
  (a classifier follow-up errors → pages stay unrouted). The report is the
  visible heartbeat that catches failures and surfaces judgment-only cases
  (new-leaf candidates, label staleness) that automation deliberately won't touch.
- **Why stable leaf `id`s:** the system is meant to be reorganized repeatedly.
  Keying assignments on leaf *paths* makes every rename a fragile mass-rewrite.
  An immutable `id` per leaf (path = location only) lets the reconciler diff trees
  by id — unambiguous rename/split/merge/delete detection — so reorg is cheap and
  safe to repeat. Page frontmatter keeps using readable *paths*; the reconciler
  uses id-continuity to migrate those paths.
- **Why not fold all of this into the bundled consolidation prompt:** the
  maintainer runs a *custom* consolidation prompt via
  `config.memory.v2.consolidation_prompt_path`. The assignment step is added to
  *her* prompt (a workspace file) — zero blast radius on the bundled prompt or
  other installs. Only the loader/index/job changes are code.

## Verified integration points (current code)

- v3 loader: `src/memory/v3/tree.ts` — `resolveDataDir()` (32-36) →
  `<workspace>/memory/v3/data/`; `loadLeafTree(dataDir)` (99-137) builds `byPage`
  from `assignments.json` (`Record<Slug, LeafPath[]>`, line 126).
- Leaf schema: `src/memory/v3/types.ts:14-17` `LeafFrontmatter { path, in_core }`;
  parser `tree.ts:68-83`.
- Page frontmatter: `src/memory/v2/page-index.ts` (reads `summary`/`edges`/`ref_files`),
  `src/memory/v2/page-store.ts:202-231` (`parsePageContent`/`renderPageContent`,
  roundtrips unknown fields → `leaves:` additive-safe), schema in
  `src/memory/v2/types.ts` (`ConceptPageFrontmatter`).
- Needle: `src/memory/v3/needle.ts:40-115` `buildNeedleIndex` (no rebuild API);
  lazy lanes in `src/memory/v3/shadow-plugin.ts:93,129-139`, test reset at 96-98.
- Consolidation follow-up: `src/memory/v2/consolidation-job.ts:98-100`
  (`FOLLOW_UP_JOB_TYPES = ["memory_v2_reembed"]`), enqueue loop at 204; prompt
  resolved 173-176 and passed to `runBackgroundJob` at 170.
- Jobs: `src/memory/jobs-store.ts:17-51` (`MemoryJobType`; legacy v3 types 48-50),
  `src/memory/jobs-worker.ts:515-634` (dispatch switch), 684-690 (checkpoints),
  716-790 (`maybeEnqueueGraphMaintenanceJobs`).
- Flags: `src/memory/v3/shadow-plugin.ts:67-68` (`memory-v3-shadow`,
  `memory-v3-live`), predicate `isAssistantFeatureFlagEnabled`.
- Telemetry: `src/memory/migrations/268-add-memory-v3-selections.ts` (slug-keyed).
- Workspace migrations: `src/workspace/migrations/registry.ts` (WORKSPACE_MIGRATIONS),
  example `089-move-memory-tree-out-of-v3.ts`.
- CLI: only `src/cli/commands/memory-v2.ts` exists; no `memory-v3.ts` yet.

---

## PR 1: Add optional stable `id` to leaf frontmatter

### Depends on
None

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-1-leaf-id-schema

### Title
feat(memory-v3): add optional stable `id` to leaf frontmatter schema

### Files
- src/memory/v3/types.ts
- src/memory/v3/tree.ts
- src/memory/v3/__tests__/tree.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. In `types.ts`, extend `LeafFrontmatter` with `id?: string` (optional for
   backward compat — existing leaves lack it). Add `id?: string` to `LeafNode`.
2. In `tree.ts` `parseLeafFrontmatter`, parse `record.id` when it is a string;
   tolerate its absence (do not throw). Carry it onto the returned frontmatter.
   In `loadLeafTree`, copy `frontmatter.id` onto the `LeafNode`.
3. Tests: a leaf with `id:` parses and exposes it; a leaf without `id:` still
   parses (id undefined). Use generic leaf paths (`domain-a/topic-x`).

### Acceptance criteria
- `LeafFrontmatter.id` is optional; loader exposes it when present.
- Existing id-less leaves load unchanged (no throw).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; scoped tests pass.

## PR 2: Read `leaves:` from page frontmatter into the page index

### Depends on
None

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-2-page-index-leaves

### Title
feat(memory): surface page `leaves:` frontmatter in the page index

### Files
- src/memory/v2/types.ts
- src/memory/v2/page-index.ts
- src/memory/v2/__tests__/page-index.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. In `types.ts`, add `leaves?: string[]` to `ConceptPageFrontmatter` (additive,
   optional). `parsePageContent` already roundtrips unknown fields, so existing
   pages are unaffected.
2. In `page-index.ts`, read `leaves` from each page's frontmatter into the
   `PageIndexEntry` (alongside `summary`/`edges`). Default to `[]` when absent.
   No consumer yet — purely additive plumbing.
3. Tests: a page with `leaves: [a, b]` exposes them in its index entry; a page
   without the field exposes `[]`.

### Acceptance criteria
- `PageIndexEntry.leaves` is populated from frontmatter; absent → `[]`.
- No behavior change for existing pages; `tsc` clean; scoped tests pass.

## PR 3: Needle index rebuild/invalidation API

### Depends on
None

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-3-needle-rebuild

### Title
feat(memory-v3): add a rebuild/invalidate hook for the needle index and lanes

### Files
- src/memory/v3/shadow-plugin.ts
- src/memory/v3/__tests__/shadow-plugin.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. Generalize the test-only `resetShadowLanesForTests` (line 96-98) into a
   non-test `invalidateLanes()` that clears the memoized `lanesPromise` so the
   next `getLanes(config)` rebuilds (tree reload + fresh `buildNeedleIndex`).
   Keep the test reset as a thin wrapper (or alias) to avoid churn.
2. Export `invalidateLanes()` for use by the maintenance job (PR 7) and the
   reconciler (PR 12).
3. Tests: after `invalidateLanes()`, the next `getLanes` triggers a rebuild
   (assert via a build-count spy or a changed fixture being picked up).

### Acceptance criteria
- `invalidateLanes()` forces a one-time rebuild on next `getLanes`.
- Concurrent first-callers still share a single build (memoization intact).
- `tsc` clean; scoped tests pass.

## PR 4: Loader derives `byPage` from page frontmatter (assignments.json fallback)

### Depends on
PR 2

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-4-loader-frontmatter

### Title
feat(memory-v3): build the assignment index from page `leaves:` with json fallback

### Files
- src/memory/v3/tree.ts
- src/memory/v3/__tests__/tree.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. Change `loadLeafTree(dataDir, pageLeaves?)` to accept an optional
   `pageLeaves: Map<Slug, LeafPath[]>` (supplied by orchestrators from the
   page index; keeps `loadLeafTree` testable with explicit inputs).
2. Build `byPage`/`members` precedence: for each slug, **frontmatter `leaves:`
   wins**; for slugs absent from `pageLeaves` (or with empty `leaves`), fall back
   to `assignments.json`. Union is not needed here (per-page precedence) — the
   union happens at write time (PR 6).
3. When `pageLeaves` is omitted (bundled stub, tests), behave exactly as today
   (assignments.json only) — fully backward compatible.
4. Update the orchestrator/caller (`shadow-plugin.ts` init) to pass the page
   index's `leaves` map into `loadLeafTree`.
5. Tests: a page with frontmatter `leaves:` routes by it even if `assignments.json`
   disagrees; a page only in `assignments.json` still routes; stub-only path
   unchanged.

### Acceptance criteria
- Frontmatter `leaves:` is the source of truth; `assignments.json` is fallback.
- Omitting `pageLeaves` preserves current behavior byte-for-byte.
- `tsc` clean; scoped tests pass.

## PR 5: One-time backfill of `leaves:` into page frontmatter

### Depends on
PR 2

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-5-backfill-leaves-migration

### Title
feat(workspace): backfill v3 `leaves:` into page frontmatter from assignments.json

### Files
- src/workspace/migrations/0NN-backfill-v3-leaves.ts  (next sequential id)
- src/workspace/migrations/registry.ts
- src/workspace/migrations/__tests__/backfill-v3-leaves.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. New `WorkspaceMigration` (copy the `089` shape: `{id, description,
   retryFailedCheckpoint, run, down}`). In `run(workspaceDir)`: if
   `<workspace>/memory/v3/data/assignments.json` exists, read it; for each slug,
   load the concept page, and if its frontmatter has no `leaves:` (or empty),
   write `leaves:` = the assignment. **Idempotent:** skip pages that already
   carry `leaves:` (don't clobber the maintainer's edits).
2. Use the existing page read/write (`parsePageContent`/`renderPageContent`) so
   the rest of the frontmatter is preserved.
3. Append to `WORKSPACE_MIGRATIONS`. `down` is a no-op (additive field; safe to
   leave) or strips the field — prefer no-op to avoid data loss.
4. Tests: pages gain `leaves:` matching assignments; pages with pre-existing
   `leaves:` are untouched; re-run is a no-op.

### Acceptance criteria
- After migration, every assigned page carries `leaves:` matching assignments.json.
- Pre-existing `leaves:` preserved; migration idempotent.
- `tsc` clean; scoped migration test passes.

## PR 6: Classifier-union module (`assignPages`)

### Depends on
PR 2

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-6-assign-union

### Title
feat(memory-v3): classifier that unions leaf assignments into page frontmatter

### Files
- src/memory/v3/assign.ts
- src/memory/v3/__tests__/assign.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. New `assignPages(opts)` that, for a set of target slugs (default: pages whose
   `leaves:` is empty/missing): renders the leaf tree as a numbered, cache-stable
   system prefix (`[N] <path> — <label>`), classifies each page via
   `getConfiguredProvider("memoryV3RouteL1")` (reuse the existing v3 route
   callsite), forcing a tool that returns `selected_ids: integer[]`; map ids →
   leaf paths by 1-based index.
2. **Union semantics:** read the page's existing `leaves:` frontmatter and write
   back `union(existing, classified)` — never overwrite. Out-of-range/0 ids
   dropped; a page that fails classification is left unchanged (recall-safe).
3. Provider safety: respect a passed provider/profile so callers can force
   non-Gemini; bounded `maxTokens`, thinking off; throttle between calls.
4. Return a structured result (per-slug before/after leaves, failures) for the
   job + health report to consume.
5. Tests: union preserves prior picks and adds new ones; failure leaves the page
   unchanged; deterministic id→path mapping; generic slugs/leaves only.

### Acceptance criteria
- New/empty pages get classified; existing picks are unioned, never overwritten.
- Classification failure is non-destructive (page keeps prior `leaves:`).
- `tsc` clean; scoped tests pass.

## PR 7: `memory_v3_maintain` job handler

### Depends on
PR 3, PR 6

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-7-maintain-job

### Title
feat(memory-v3): add the memory_v3_maintain job (classify-union → needle rebuild → prune)

### Files
- src/memory/v3/maintain-job.ts
- src/memory/jobs-store.ts
- src/memory/jobs-worker.ts
- src/memory/v3/__tests__/maintain-job.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. Add `"memory_v3_maintain"` to the `MemoryJobType` union (jobs-store.ts, near
   the active types — **not** the legacy block at 48-50; those stay quarantined).

### Implementation steps
1. New `memory v3` command group (mirror `memory-v2.ts` structure) with verbs:
   `reconcile` (run PR 12 against the current edited tree vs the last snapshot),
   `rename-leaf`/`move-leaf`/`split-leaf`/`merge-leaves`/`delete-leaf`/`add-leaf`
   (thin wrappers that edit the leaf files then call reconcile), `set-core`
   (edit `core.json`; **validate** all entries exist; **preview** the resulting
   always-on page count before writing), `health` (print `renderV3Health`),
   `rebuild-index` (`invalidateLanes`).
2. Route execution through the daemon over IPC (the daemon owns the live tree),
   following the existing route pattern. No new *agent* tool registrations — these
   are CLI/daemon ops only.

   `reconcile` invokes the reconciler + snapshot; `health` renders the report.

### Acceptance criteria
- Gardening verbs reconcile safely (snapshot + integrity validation).
- `set-core` validates + previews always-on page count; writes only on confirm.
- `tsc` clean; scoped tests pass.

---

## Workspace change (not a code PR)

**Maintainer's custom consolidation prompt** (`config.memory.v2.consolidation_prompt_path`):
add a step instructing the assistant, after creating/updating each page, to set
its `leaves:` frontmatter (best effort, from the leaf tree she can read under
`memory/v3/data/leaves/`). She does the context-rich picks; the post-consolidation
`memory_v3_maintain` job unions in the rest. This is a workspace file edit,
deployed during the migration runbook — never committed to the repo, never
touches the bundled prompt.

## Migration runbook (operational, run once at adoption)

1. **Quiesce consolidation.** Raise her consolidation interval to ~24h *and*
   raise `consolidation_max_buffer_lines` (the size trigger fires independently of
   the interval), or simply perform the swap inside a known-quiet window. Record
   the original values to restore later.
2. **Backfill current.** Re-run the delta scan + classifier-union so
   `assignments.json` / page `leaves:` cover everything created since the last
   backfill (the corpus moves; do this immediately before the swap). Verify:
   delta scan reports 0 unassigned.
3. **Swap in the new custom consolidation prompt** (adds the `leaves:` step).
4. **Manual verification run.** Trigger one consolidation manually
   (`POST /consolidation/run-now`). Confirm: new pages carry `leaves:`; the
   `memory_v3_maintain` follow-up ran (union + needle rebuild); re-run the delta
   scan → **0 unassigned + needle current**; spot-check a page carries *both* her
   picks and classifier picks (union fired).
5. **Restore cadence.** Return the interval + buffer-line threshold to their
   original values (or intentionally adopt a new cadence).
6. **Ongoing.** Every consolidation now self-maintains; the health block surfaces
   anything that needs her judgment (new leaves, label refresh, failures).

## Out of scope (future)

- Auto-refreshing leaf **labels** to mention new entities — labels are canon;
  this needs `last_human_edit_at` tracking + maintainer ratification (the health
  report flags candidates; it does not rewrite labels).
- Salience-weighted working-set eviction; needle-lane source attribution.
- Auto-triggered tree restructuring — gardening stays a deliberate, maintainer-run
  act fed by the health report, never automatic.
- Dropping `assignments.json` entirely — kept as a derived export/fallback during
  the transition; revisit after frontmatter is the sole source in practice.

</details>

## Self-review + integrated verification (lead) ✅ — final

3 fresh-eyes passes (faithfulness, integration, slop) → **5 gaps found & fixed** (#32717–#32721): de-dup'd the `memory_v3_maintain` consolidation enqueue (was 2×, broke its own test), registered the orphaned leaf-id migration (renumbered 093), pointed CLI `health`/`set-core` at the authoritative `leaves:` frontmatter, made `reconcile` help honest, and wired the maintenance interval backstop.

### Verification result
- **`bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean** (fully-installed worktree).
- **All 18 `src/memory/v3/` test files + the 3 touched non-v3 files pass in isolation:** consolidation-job 21/0, backfill-leaf-ids 6/0, memory-v3 CLI 7/0, jobs-worker-v2-schedule 15/0, tree 10/0, maintain-job 7/0, router (isolated) green, shadow-plugin (isolated) green, live-integration 4/0, etc.
- **Full `src/memory/v3/` directory sweep is RED (≈19 fail) due to a test-harness mock leak, not product code.**

### Why the sweep is red (diagnosed, not product defects)
1. bun runs `live-integration.test.ts` first; in a worktree where `packages/service-contracts` wasn't `bun install`-ed, it throws `Cannot find module '@vellumai/service-contracts/credential-rpc'` as an **unhandled error between tests**, aborting that file mid-run.
2. Because it aborts, its process-global `mock.module("../../../providers/provider-send-message.js")` is **never torn down** and **leaks into every subsequent file** in the same bun process — so `router`, `shadow-plugin`, `tree`, `maintain-job` see the real provider / a stale spy and fail, despite passing standalone. (Counts even drift run-to-run — classic cross-file state bleed.)

Neither cause is a defect in this PR's product code: `credential-rpc` is a normal source export that resolves in a properly-installed checkout, and every file is green alone. **This branch did, however, add new v3 test files using the same un-guarded `mock.module` pattern** that several pre-existing v3 tests (`orchestrate`/`router`/`selector`/`live-integration`, all unchanged here) already use.

### Recommended follow-up (separate PR, test-only)
Make the v3 tests' `mock.module` installs restore-on-teardown (delegate-to-real-unless-flag, per the repo's known bun mock-leak pattern) so `bun test src/memory/v3/` is green under a single-process sweep. Tracked as a fast-follow; does not block this PR (product code verified, tsc clean, all files green in isolation).

Presented for manual review — not auto-merged.

payload.body:
<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Memory v3 — Self-Maintaining Structure</summary>

# Memory v3 — Self-Maintaining Structure

## Overview

Make the memory-v3 topic tree **self-maintaining** so it stays coherent as the
corpus grows and reorganizes over weeks/months, without a human babysitting a
batch script. The maintainer (the assistant) keeps her own structure current as
a natural extension of how she already consolidates memory; deterministic
plumbing keeps referential integrity; a green-suppressed health report surfaces
the cases automation can't resolve.

Four capabilities, mirroring how v2 consolidation already works (an assistant
turn for judgment + a mechanical follow-up for indexing):

1. **Assignment stays current** — page→leaf assignment lives in page frontmatter
   (`leaves:`), exactly like v2's `edges:`. The maintainer sets it as she files a
   page; a post-consolidation classifier **unions in** anything she missed; the
   needle index rebuilds. Drift becomes structurally hard.
2. **Health report** — at the consolidation trigger, a flag-gated block reports
   coverage gaps, pipeline failures, and judgment-only candidates (new leaves,
   stale labels). Shown only when something is actionable.
3. **Tree gardening** — the maintainer can restructure the tree (add / rename /
   move / split / merge / delete leaves). A deterministic reconciler keeps all
   references intact, re-homes pages so none are orphaned, and snapshots for
   rollback. Stable leaf `id`s make reorg cheap and safe to repeat.
4. **Core editing** — the maintainer owns the always-on `core.json` set, with
   validation and an always-on page-count/cost preview.

## Design rationale (the "why")

- **Why frontmatter, not `assignments.json`:** v2 already stores structural links
  (`edges:`) in page frontmatter as the single source of truth — no side table.
  Mirroring that makes assignment *born with the page and maintained with it*, so
  it can't silently drift. `assignments.json` becomes a derived/fallback export,
  not the source.
- **Why union (maintainer ∪ classifier):** the maintainer read the source
  material and has context a summary-only classifier lacks (cross-domain links,
  nuance); the classifier systematically sweeps all leaves and catches the
  obvious homes she skips mid-consolidation. Unioning their picks yields strictly
  higher recall than either alone, consistent with the multi-home design. Cost:
  multi-home creeps from ~3.2 toward ~4–5 leaves/page — acceptable; L2 + the
  working-set cap absorb it.
- **Why a health report even with auto-classify:** automation can fail silently
  (a classifier follow-up errors → pages stay unrouted). The report is the
  visible heartbeat that catches failures and surfaces judgment-only cases
  (new-leaf candidates, label staleness) that automation deliberately won't touch.
- **Why stable leaf `id`s:** the system is meant to be reorganized repeatedly.
  Keying assignments on leaf *paths* makes every rename a fragile mass-rewrite.
  An immutable `id` per leaf (path = location only) lets the reconciler diff trees
  by id — unambiguous rename/split/merge/delete detection — so reorg is cheap and
  safe to repeat. Page frontmatter keeps using readable *paths*; the reconciler
  uses id-continuity to migrate those paths.
- **Why not fold all of this into the bundled consolidation prompt:** the
  maintainer runs a *custom* consolidation prompt via
  `config.memory.v2.consolidation_prompt_path`. The assignment step is added to
  *her* prompt (a workspace file) — zero blast radius on the bundled prompt or
  other installs. Only the loader/index/job changes are code.

## Verified integration points (current code)

- v3 loader: `src/memory/v3/tree.ts` — `resolveDataDir()` (32-36) →
  `<workspace>/memory/v3/data/`; `loadLeafTree(dataDir)` (99-137) builds `byPage`
  from `assignments.json` (`Record<Slug, LeafPath[]>`, line 126).
- Leaf schema: `src/memory/v3/types.ts:14-17` `LeafFrontmatter { path, in_core }`;
  parser `tree.ts:68-83`.
- Page frontmatter: `src/memory/v2/page-index.ts` (reads `summary`/`edges`/`ref_files`),
  `src/memory/v2/page-store.ts:202-231` (`parsePageContent`/`renderPageContent`,
  roundtrips unknown fields → `leaves:` additive-safe), schema in
  `src/memory/v2/types.ts` (`ConceptPageFrontmatter`).
- Needle: `src/memory/v3/needle.ts:40-115` `buildNeedleIndex` (no rebuild API);
  lazy lanes in `src/memory/v3/shadow-plugin.ts:93,129-139`, test reset at 96-98.
- Consolidation follow-up: `src/memory/v2/consolidation-job.ts:98-100`
  (`FOLLOW_UP_JOB_TYPES = ["memory_v2_reembed"]`), enqueue loop at 204; prompt
  resolved 173-176 and passed to `runBackgroundJob` at 170.
- Jobs: `src/memory/jobs-store.ts:17-51` (`MemoryJobType`; legacy v3 types 48-50),
  `src/memory/jobs-worker.ts:515-634` (dispatch switch), 684-690 (checkpoints),
  716-790 (`maybeEnqueueGraphMaintenanceJobs`).
- Flags: `src/memory/v3/shadow-plugin.ts:67-68` (`memory-v3-shadow`,
  `memory-v3-live`), predicate `isAssistantFeatureFlagEnabled`.
- Telemetry: `src/memory/migrations/268-add-memory-v3-selections.ts` (slug-keyed).
- Workspace migrations: `src/workspace/migrations/registry.ts` (WORKSPACE_MIGRATIONS),
  example `089-move-memory-tree-out-of-v3.ts`.
- CLI: only `src/cli/commands/memory-v2.ts` exists; no `memory-v3.ts` yet.

---

## PR 1: Add optional stable `id` to leaf frontmatter

### Depends on
None

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-1-leaf-id-schema

### Title
feat(memory-v3): add optional stable `id` to leaf frontmatter schema

### Files
- src/memory/v3/types.ts
- src/memory/v3/tree.ts
- src/memory/v3/__tests__/tree.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. In `types.ts`, extend `LeafFrontmatter` with `id?: string` (optional for
   backward compat — existing leaves lack it). Add `id?: string` to `LeafNode`.
2. In `tree.ts` `parseLeafFrontmatter`, parse `record.id` when it is a string;
   tolerate its absence (do not throw). Carry it onto the returned frontmatter.
   In `loadLeafTree`, copy `frontmatter.id` onto the `LeafNode`.
3. Tests: a leaf with `id:` parses and exposes it; a leaf without `id:` still
   parses (id undefined). Use generic leaf paths (`domain-a/topic-x`).

### Acceptance criteria
- `LeafFrontmatter.id` is optional; loader exposes it when present.
- Existing id-less leaves load unchanged (no throw).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; scoped tests pass.

## PR 2: Read `leaves:` from page frontmatter into the page index

### Depends on
None

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-2-page-index-leaves

### Title
feat(memory): surface page `leaves:` frontmatter in the page index

### Files

- src/memory/v2/page-index.ts
- src/memory/v2/__tests__/page-index.test.ts

1. In `types.ts`, add `leaves?: string[]` to `ConceptPageFrontmatter` (additive,

2. In `page-index.ts`, read `leaves` from each page's frontmatter into the

   No consumer yet — purely additive plumbing.

## PR 3: Needle index rebuild/invalidation API

### Depends on
None

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-3-needle-rebuild

### Title
feat(memory-v3): add a rebuild/invalidate hook for the needle index and lanes

### Files
- src/memory/v3/shadow-plugin.ts
- src/memory/v3/__tests__/shadow-plugin.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. Generalize the test-only `resetShadowLanesForTests` (line 96-98) into a
   non-test `invalidateLanes()` that clears the memoized `lanesPromise` so the
   next `getLanes(config)` rebuilds (tree reload + fresh `buildNeedleIndex`).
   Keep the test reset as a thin wrapper (or alias) to avoid churn.
2. Export `invalidateLanes()` for use by the maintenance job (PR 7) and the
   reconciler (PR 12).
3. Tests: after `invalidateLanes()`, the next `getLanes` triggers a rebuild
   (assert via a build-count spy or a changed fixture being picked up).

- `invalidateLanes()` forces a one-time rebuild on next `getLanes`.

## PR 4: Loader derives `byPage` from page frontmatter (assignments.json fallback)

### Depends on
PR 2

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-4-loader-frontmatter

### Title
feat(memory-v3): build the assignment index from page `leaves:` with json fallback

### Files

- src/memory/v3/__tests__/tree.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. Change `loadLeafTree(dataDir, pageLeaves?)` to accept an optional

## PR 5: One-time backfill of `leaves:` into page frontmatter

### Depends on
PR 2

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-5-backfill-leaves-migration

### Title
feat(workspace): backfill v3 `leaves:` into page frontmatter from assignments.json

### Files

## PR 6: Classifier-union module (`assignPages`)

### Depends on
PR 2

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-6-assign-union

### Title
feat(memory-v3): classifier that unions leaf assignments into page frontmatter

### Files
- src/memory/v3/assign.ts
- src/memory/v3/__tests__/assign.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. New `assignPages(opts)` that, for a set of target slugs (default: pages whose
   `leaves:` is empty/missing): renders the leaf tree as a numbered, cache-stable
   system prefix (`[N] <path> — <label>`), classifies each page via
   `getConfiguredProvider("memoryV3RouteL1")` (reuse the existing v3 route
   callsite), forcing a tool that returns `selected_ids: integer[]`; map ids →
   leaf paths by 1-based index.
2. **Union semantics:** read the page's existing `leaves:` frontmatter and write
   back `union(existing, classified)` — never overwrite. Out-of-range/0 ids
   dropped; a page that fails classification is left unchanged (recall-safe).
3. Provider safety: respect a passed provider/profile so callers can force
   non-Gemini; bounded `maxTokens`, thinking off; throttle between calls.
4. Return a structured result (per-slug before/after leaves, failures) for the
   job + health report to consume.
5. Tests: union preserves prior picks and adds new ones; failure leaves the page
   unchanged; deterministic id→path mapping; generic slugs/leaves only.

### Acceptance criteria
- New/empty pages get classified; existing picks are unioned, never overwritten.
- Classification failure is non-destructive (page keeps prior `leaves:`).
- `tsc` clean; scoped tests pass.

- src/workspace/migrations/registry.ts
- src/workspace/migrations/__tests__/backfill-leaf-ids.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. New `WorkspaceMigration`: for every `<workspace>/memory/v3/data/leaves/**/*.md`
   lacking `id:`, write a stable id into frontmatter. Generate the id
   deterministically (e.g. a short hash of the *current* path at backfill time)
   so re-runs are stable; **skip leaves that already have `id:`** (idempotent).
2. Preserve the rest of the frontmatter and body (parse → set id → re-serialize).
3. Append to `WORKSPACE_MIGRATIONS`; `down` no-op.
4. Tests: every leaf gains a unique stable id; pre-existing ids untouched; re-run

## PR 12: Tree reconciler (diff-by-id, rewrite refs, re-home, prune, validate)

### Depends on
PR 1, PR 6, PR 11, PR 13

### Branch
mem-v3-self-maint/pr-12-reconciler

### Title
feat(memory-v3): deterministic tree reconciler for safe restructuring

### Files
- src/memory/v3/reconcile.ts
- src/memory/v3/__tests__/reconcile.test.ts

### Implementation steps
1. `reconcileTree(prevSnapshot, currentDataDir, pageIndex)`:
   - Diff previous vs current leaves **by `id`**: `id` in both but path changed →
     **rename/move** (rewrite every page `leaves:` ref from old→new path, and
     `core.json` entries). `id` removed → **delete** (re-home its member pages via
     `assignPages` before dropping refs; never orphan). `id` newly present → add.
     Maintainer marks a **split** (one id → two new leaves) → re-home members
     across the new leaves via `assignPages`.
   - **Prune** `core.json` entries that point at non-existent leaves.
   - **Validate**: no page `leaves:` ref, and no core entry, points at a missing
     leaf path. Throw `RouteError` on any residual dangling ref (caller restores
     from snapshot — PR 13).

2. Take a snapshot (PR 13) before mutating; on validation failure, restore.
3. Call `invalidateLanes()` after a successful reconcile.
4. Tests: rename preserves assignments (refs rewritten); delete re-homes with no
   orphan; split distributes members; dangling core pruned; validation catches an
   injected dangling ref and triggers restore. Generic leaves only.

### Acceptance criteria

- Validation fails closed and restores from snapshot.

### Depends on
PR 12, PR 13

### Branch

### Implementation steps
1. New `memory v3` command group (mirror `memory-v2.ts` structure) with verbs:
   `reconcile` (run PR 12 against the current edited tree vs the last snapshot),
   `rename-leaf`/`move-leaf`/`split-leaf`/`merge-leaves`/`delete-leaf`/`add-leaf`
   (thin wrappers that edit the leaf files then call reconcile), `set-core`
   (edit `core.json`; **validate** all entries exist; **preview** the resulting
   always-on page count before writing), `health` (print `renderV3Health`),
   `rebuild-index` (`invalidateLanes`).
2. Route execution through the daemon over IPC (the daemon owns the live tree),
   following the existing route pattern. No new *agent* tool registrations — these
   are CLI/daemon ops only.
3. Tests: `set-core` rejects unknown leaves and prints the cost preview;
   `reconcile` invokes the reconciler + snapshot; `health` renders the report.

### Acceptance criteria
- Gardening verbs reconcile safely (snapshot + integrity validation).
- `set-core` validates + previews always-on page count; writes only on confirm.

## Workspace change (not a code PR)

**Maintainer's custom consolidation prompt** (`config.memory.v2.consolidation_prompt_path`):
add a step instructing the assistant, after creating/updating each page, to set
its `leaves:` frontmatter (best effort, from the leaf tree she can read under
`memory/v3/data/leaves/`). She does the context-rich picks; the post-consolidation
`memory_v3_maintain` job unions in the rest. This is a workspace file edit,
deployed during the migration runbook — never committed to the repo, never
touches the bundled prompt.

## Migration runbook (operational, run once at adoption)

1. **Quiesce consolidation.** Raise her consolidation interval to ~24h *and*
   raise `consolidation_max_buffer_lines` (the size trigger fires independently of
   the interval), or simply perform the swap inside a known-quiet window. Record
   the original values to restore later.
2. **Backfill current.** Re-run the delta scan + classifier-union so
   `assignments.json` / page `leaves:` cover everything created since the last
   backfill (the corpus moves; do this immediately before the swap). Verify:
   delta scan reports 0 unassigned.
3. **Swap in the new custom consolidation prompt** (adds the `leaves:` step).
4. **Manual verification run.** Trigger one consolidation manually
   (`POST /consolidation/run-now`). Confirm: new pages carry `leaves:`; the
   `memory_v3_maintain` follow-up ran (union + needle rebuild); re-run the delta
   scan → **0 unassigned + needle current**; spot-check a page carries *both* her
   picks and classifier picks (union fired).
5. **Restore cadence.** Return the interval + buffer-line threshold to their
   original values (or intentionally adopt a new cadence).
6. **Ongoing.** Every consolidation now self-maintains; the health block surfaces
   anything that needs her judgment (new leaves, label refresh, failures).

## Out of scope (future)

- Auto-refreshing leaf **labels** to mention new entities — labels are canon;
  this needs `last_human_edit_at` tracking + maintainer ratification (the health
  report flags candidates; it does not rewrite labels).
- Salience-weighted working-set eviction; needle-lane source attribution.
- Auto-triggered tree restructuring — gardening stays a deliberate, maintainer-run
  act fed by the health report, never automatic.
- Dropping `assignments.json` entirely — kept as a derived export/fallback during
  the transition; revisit after frontmatter is the sole source in practice.

</details>

## Second pass — addresses Codex P2 + CI Type Check

**Codex feedback addressed** ([comment](https://github.com/vellum-ai/vellum-assistant/pull/32677#discussion_r3329067798))

History payloads reference `toolCalls` / `surfaces` *positionally* — the renderer (`resolveToolCall`, `resolveSurface` in `transcript-message-body.tsx`) falls back to `parseInt(id, 10) → array[idx]` when the id matches no real member id. The first pass concatenated `toolCalls` / `surfaces` arrays but left donor `{ type: "tool", id: "0" }` / `{ type: "surface", id: "0" }` entries unchanged, so on the folded long-turn bubble the donor entries resolved to the survivor's `toolCalls[0]` / `surfaces[0]` — wrong progress card / wrong surface at every page boundary.

**Fix:** `remapAdjacentContentOrder` now shifts positional ids for all four kinds (text, attachment, tool/toolCall, surface) by the survivor's corresponding array length. Streaming-shape entries that carry a real id (`toolu_…`, surfaceId UUIDs) bypass the shift via a `/^\d+$/` gate — they resolve via the id-keyed first-pass lookup, so any remap would corrupt them.

**CI Type Check fix:** `DisplayAttachment` requires `previewUrl` — added `previewUrl: null` to the three test fixtures that omitted it.

**Tests:** 3 new cases under `mergeAdjacentAssistantMessages · contentOrder remap`:
- `shifts tool:N positional ids in the donor by survivor.toolCalls.length (history shape)`
- `shifts surface:N positional ids in the donor by survivor.surfaces.length (history shape)`
- `leaves real (non-numeric) toolCall / surface ids untouched (streaming shape)`

Plus the existing `interleaved text + tool positional entries remap each by their own offset` updated to exercise both offsets simultaneously.

**Verification**
- `bun test src/domains/chat/utils/message-merge.test.ts` → 18/18 pass
- All 7 CI checks green on `8259bd8717` ✅

<details>
<summary>Plan papertrail: Memory v3 — Live Injection Mode</summary>

# Memory v3 — Live Injection Mode

## Overview

Make memory-v3 an actual injection source (not just shadow telemetry) behind a
new **default-off** `memory-v3-live` feature flag, distinct from
`memory-v3-shadow`. When on for a conversation, the v3 orchestrator's
`finalInjection` becomes the injected `<memory>` block — **suppressing v2's
injection** so there is exactly one memory source — with two supporting
disciplines: (1) the `<memory>` block is stripped from **all** historical user
messages each turn (keeps the context window lean and makes history
byte-stable/cacheable), and (2) the provider call is told the latest user
message is volatile so the prompt-cache anchor lands on the most recent
**stable** message instead of the changing current turn.

**v2 is left completely untouched.** Every change is gated on `memory-v3-live`;
when the flag is off, the v2 injection path, its last-message-only strip, and
its cache-anchor behavior are bit-for-bit identical to today. The flag flip,
A/B, and cutover remain operational follow-ups outside this plan — this plan
ends with live injection fully implemented and primed behind a default-off
flag.

The foundational provider change (PR L1) is a **standalone, v2-safe**
generalization of cache-anchor placement that is independently useful and
mergeable on its own; it does not depend on any other PR here.

## PR L1: Provider cache-anchor flag for a volatile trailing user message

### Depends on
None

### Branch
memory-v3-live/pr-l1-cache-anchor-flag

### Title
feat(providers): add mutableLatestUserMessage cache-anchor option

### Files
- `assistant/src/providers/types.ts`
- `assistant/src/providers/anthropic/client.ts`
- `assistant/src/__tests__/anthropic-provider.test.ts`

### Implementation steps
1. Add an optional field to `SendMessageConfig` in `providers/types.ts`:
   `mutableLatestUserMessage?: boolean` with a docstring: "When true, the most
   recent user message's content varies across otherwise-identical turns (e.g. a
   per-turn memory block was injected into it). The provider places the primary
   long-TTL cache breakpoint on the most recent *stable* user message instead of
   the volatile latest one, so the cached prefix stays reusable across turns.
   Default false — existing behavior."
2. In `anthropic/client.ts`, read it next to the existing `disableTurnStartCache`
   / `cacheTtl` reads (~line 827): `const mutableLatestUserMessage = (config as
   Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.mutableLatestUserMessage === true;`.
3. In the cache-breakpoint block (the `findUserTextMsgIdx` / `turnStartIdx`
   region, ~lines 1117-1166): when `mutableLatestUserMessage` is true AND this is
   the first request of a turn (`turnStartIdx === msgs.length - 1`), do NOT apply
   the long-TTL breakpoint to `turnStartIdx` (it is volatile); the existing
   previous-turn anchor (the `findUserTextMsgIdx(turnStartIdx - 1)` path) becomes
   the primary stable anchor. During tool-use loops (`turnStartIdx <
   msgs.length - 1`) behavior is unchanged — the injected block is fixed for the
   duration of a turn, so intra-turn caching is unaffected. Preserve the existing
   4-breakpoint budget accounting.
4. Leave `disableTurnStartCache` semantics intact and independent — do not
   overload it. The two flags may co-resolve to similar placement today but
   express different intents.
5. Tests in `anthropic-provider.test.ts`:
   - With `mutableLatestUserMessage: true` on a first-of-turn request, the
     turn-start (latest) user message receives NO long-TTL breakpoint and the
     previous stable user message does.
   - With the flag absent/false, breakpoint placement is byte-identical to
     current behavior (guard against v2 regressions).
   - During a tool-use loop (turn-start not last), the flag does not change
     placement.
   - First-turn-of-conversation (no previous user message) degrades gracefully
     (no throw; at most a one-turn cache-write cost).

### Acceptance criteria
- `mutableLatestUserMessage` is a documented optional `SendMessageConfig` field,
  default-off.
- When off, every existing caller (including v2) is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- When on, the long-TTL anchor moves off the volatile latest message to the most
  recent stable user message on first-of-turn requests only.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; the new and existing provider tests pass.

## PR L2: Register memory-v3-live feature flag (default off)

### Depends on
None

### Branch
memory-v3-live/pr-l2-register-live-flag

### Title
feat(feature-flags): add memory-v3-live flag (default off)

### Files
- `meta/feature-flags/feature-flag-registry.json`
- bundled copies via `meta/feature-flags/sync-bundled-copies.ts`
- `meta/feature-flags/PENDING_PLATFORM_PRS.md`

### Implementation steps
1. Add an assistant-scope entry mirroring `memory-v3-shadow` (kebab-case `id`
   === `key`, no dots): `id`/`key` = `memory-v3-live`, `defaultEnabled: false`,
   description noting it makes v3 the live injection source (suppressing v2) and
   must only be enabled after shadow telemetry validates the design.
2. Run `bun run meta/feature-flags/sync-bundled-copies.ts`; commit regenerated
   bundled copies.
3. Record the companion Terraform requirement for `memory-v3-live` in
   `PENDING_PLATFORM_PRS.md`. Do NOT create a cross-repo PR here.

### Acceptance criteria
- Registry contains `memory-v3-live`, default off, `id` === `key`.
- Bundled copies synced; `PENDING_PLATFORM_PRS.md` updated.
- No cross-repo PR created.

## PR L3: Working-set → `<memory>` block renderer

### Depends on
None

### Branch
memory-v3-live/pr-l3-render-memory-block

### Title
feat(memory-v3): render the working-set selection as a memory block

### Files
- `assistant/src/memory/v3/render-injection.ts` (new)
- `assistant/src/memory/v3/__tests__/render-injection.test.ts` (new)

### Implementation steps
1. Create a pure function:
   ```ts
   export async function renderMemoryBlock(
     finalInjection: Slug[],
     pageContent: (slug: Slug) => Promise<string>,
   ): Promise<string>; // returns a "<memory>\n...\n</memory>" text block, or "" if empty
   ```
2. Concatenate the page contents in a deterministic order (e.g. input order)
   into a single `<memory>…</memory>` block. **Reuse the existing `<memory>`
   marker** so the existing strip machinery in `conversation-graph-memory.ts`
   already recognizes it. Return `""` for an empty selection (caller injects
   nothing).
3. Keep it provider-agnostic and side-effect-free (no DB, no provider calls) —
   `pageContent` is injected so it is unit-testable.
4. Tests: a small synthetic selection renders the expected single
   `<memory>`-wrapped block; empty selection → `""`; order is deterministic.

### Acceptance criteria
- `renderMemoryBlock` exported, pure, marker-reusing.
- Tests pass; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## PR L4: Strip memory from all historical user messages (v3-gated helper)

### Depends on
None

### Branch
memory-v3-live/pr-l4-strip-all-historical

### Title
feat(memory): add all-turns memory-strip helper (v3 live mode)

### Files
- `assistant/src/memory/graph/conversation-graph-memory.ts`
- `assistant/src/__tests__/strip-memory-injections.test.ts` (or the existing strip test location)

### Implementation steps
1. Next to the existing `stripExistingMemoryInjections` (which strips the
   `<memory>` block from the **last** user message only), add
   `stripAllMemoryInjections(messages)` that strips `<memory>` blocks from **every**
   user message. Reuse the same block-matching logic the existing stripper uses
   (the `<memory>` / `<memory __injected>` / `<memory_image>` recognition) —
   factor a shared per-message strip out of the existing function if that avoids
   duplication, but DO NOT change `stripExistingMemoryInjections`' behavior.
2. Do not wire it into any live path in this PR — it is a standalone helper that
   PR L6 calls only under the `memory-v3-live` flag. v2 continues to use the
   last-message-only stripper.
3. Tests: `stripAllMemoryInjections` removes `<memory>` from multiple historical
   user messages and leaves non-memory content intact; `stripExistingMemoryInjections`
   behavior is unchanged (regression guard).

### Acceptance criteria
- `stripAllMemoryInjections` exported; strips all user-message `<memory>` blocks.
- Existing last-only stripper unchanged.
- Tests pass; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## PR L5: Flip the v3 plugin injector to live (flag-gated)

### Depends on
PR L2, PR L3

### Branch
memory-v3-live/pr-l5-live-injector

### Title
feat(memory-v3): emit the working-set memory block when memory-v3-live is on

### Files
- `assistant/src/memory/v3/shadow-plugin.ts`
- `assistant/src/memory/v3/__tests__/shadow-plugin.test.ts`

### Implementation steps
1. In the v3 plugin's `produce()` (currently returns `null`): read both flags.
   - If `memory-v3-live` is on: run the orchestrator (or reuse the shadow run's
     result), render the block via `renderMemoryBlock(result.finalInjection, …)`
     (PR L3), and return it as the injector block at the appropriate placement
     (mirror v2's memory placement — `after-memory-prefix` / `append-user-tail`
     per `conversation-runtime-assembly.ts`). Still log to `memory_v3_selections`.
   - Else if `memory-v3-shadow` is on: existing observation-only behavior
     (orchestrate + log, return `null`).
   - Else: `null`.
2. Keep the lazy-init-once + failure-isolation (try/catch) behavior. A live-mode
   failure must fall back to returning `null` (no injection) rather than breaking
   the turn — note that v2 suppression (PR L6) must therefore key off the same
   flag, not off "did v3 produce a block", so a v3 failure doesn't silently drop
   all memory. (PR L6 owns that decision.)
3. Tests: `memory-v3-live` on → `produce()` returns the rendered `<memory>`
   block; shadow-only → returns `null` (+ logs); both off → `null`. Lazy-init
   once preserved.

### Acceptance criteria
- Live flag → injector emits the working-set `<memory>` block; shadow/off → `null`.
- Failure isolation preserved (live failure → `null`).
- Tests pass; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## PR L6: v2 suppression + wire the cache-anchor flag (integration)

### Depends on
PR L1, PR L4, PR L5

### Branch
memory-v3-live/pr-l6-v2-suppression-and-cache-wire

### Title
feat(memory): route injection to v3 and shift cache anchor when memory-v3-live is on

### Files
- `assistant/src/memory/graph/conversation-graph-memory.ts`
- `assistant/src/daemon/conversation-runtime-assembly.ts`
- relevant assembly/agent-loop test(s)

### Implementation steps
1. In the main-agent context assembly, when `memory-v3-live` is on for the
   conversation:
   - **Suppress v2 injection**: do not call `injectMemoryV2Block` /
     `injectMemoryBlock` for the v2 memory source (the v3 injector now provides
     the `<memory>` block). Ensure exactly one `<memory>` source ends up in the
     assembled context.
   - **Strip all historical turns**: use `stripAllMemoryInjections` (PR L4)
     instead of the last-only stripper for the v3 path.
   - **Signal the provider**: pass `mutableLatestUserMessage: true` (PR L1) in
     the mainAgent `sendMessage` `config` for the turn, since the latest user
     message now carries the volatile v3 block.
2. When `memory-v3-live` is off: take none of the above branches — v2 injection,
   the last-only strip, and the default cache anchor are unchanged.
3. Gate the suppression on the FLAG, not on whether the v3 injector returned a
   block, so a v3 failure (which yields `null`) does not silently produce a
   turn with no memory while also having suppressed v2. Decide and document the
   failure policy (recommended: if live is on but v3 produced nothing due to
   error, fall back to v2 injection for that turn).
4. Tests: with the flag on, exactly one `<memory>` source is present, the
   all-turns strip ran, and the mainAgent call received `mutableLatestUserMessage:
   true`; with the flag off, the assembled request is byte-for-byte identical to
   today (v2 regression guard).

### Acceptance criteria
- Flag on → v3 is the sole memory source, history stripped, cache flag set.
- Flag off → v2 path bit-for-bit identical.
- Documented v3-failure fallback (no silent memory loss).
- Tests pass; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## PR L7: Multi-turn integration test

### Depends on
PR L6

### Branch
memory-v3-live/pr-l7-multi-turn-integration

### Title
test(memory-v3): multi-turn live-injection integration

### Files
- `assistant/src/memory/v3/__tests__/live-integration.test.ts` (new)
- `assistant/src/memory/v3/__tests__/fixtures/live-turns.json` (new, synthetic)

### Implementation steps
1. Drive a synthetic multi-turn conversation with `memory-v3-live` on (mock the
   provider; reuse the orchestrate/selector mocking patterns):
   - Assert carry-forward: a page pinned in turn 1 appears in turn 2's injected
     `<memory>` block without being re-selected.
   - Assert working-set eviction is reflected in the injected block over turns.
   - Assert exactly one `<memory>` block exists in the assembled context each
     turn (no v2 double-inject).
   - Assert historical user messages have their prior `<memory>` blocks stripped
     each turn (byte-stable history).
2. Use generic synthetic fixtures only (no real content).

### Acceptance criteria
- Multi-turn carry-forward, eviction, single-source, and strip-all behaviors are
  asserted end-to-end.
- Tests pass; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Out of scope (explicit follow-ups)

- **Flipping `memory-v3-live` on for any instance**, A/B, default-on cutover,
  v2 deprecation/removal — operational, after shadow + live validation.
- **Companion Terraform flag** in vellum-assistant-platform (recorded in
  `PENDING_PLATFORM_PRS.md`).
- **Block-level cache refinement (Option X)** — append the `<memory>` block
  *after* the user's text within the same message and anchor on the text block,
  buying one extra turn of cache coverage vs the message-level shift in PR L1.
  A later optimization; PR L1's message-level shift is the v1.
- **Salience-weighted eviction**, **needle-lane source attribution**,
  **needle-index rebuild on consolidation** — independent v3 fast-follows.

</details>

## PR L5: Flip the v3 plugin injector to live (flag-gated)

### Depends on
PR L2, PR L3

### Branch
memory-v3-live/pr-l5-live-injector

### Title
feat(memory-v3): emit the working-set memory block when memory-v3-live is on

### Files
- `assistant/src/memory/v3/shadow-plugin.ts`
- `assistant/src/memory/v3/__tests__/shadow-plugin.test.ts`

### Implementation steps
1. In the v3 plugin's `produce()` (currently returns `null`): read both flags.
   - If `memory-v3-live` is on: run the orchestrator (or reuse the shadow run's
     result), render the block via `renderMemoryBlock(result.finalInjection, …)`
     (PR L3), and return it as the injector block at the appropriate placement

   failure must fall back to returning `null` (no injection) rather than breaking
   the turn — note that v2 suppression (PR L6) must therefore key off the same
   flag, not off "did v3 produce a block", so a v3 failure doesn't silently drop
   all memory. (PR L6 owns that decision.)
3. Tests: `memory-v3-live` on → `produce()` returns the rendered `<memory>`
   block; shadow-only → returns `null` (+ logs); both off → `null`. Lazy-init
   once preserved.

### Depends on
PR L1, PR L4, PR L5

### Branch

### Title

- `assistant/src/daemon/conversation-runtime-assembly.ts`

   all-turns strip ran, and the mainAgent call received `mutableLatestUserMessage:
   true`; with the flag off, the assembled request is byte-for-byte identical to
   today (v2 regression guard).

- Flag on → v3 is the sole memory source, history stripped, cache flag set.
- Flag off → v2 path bit-for-bit identical.
- Documented v3-failure fallback (no silent memory loss).
- Tests pass; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## PR L7: Multi-turn integration test

### Depends on
PR L6

### Branch
memory-v3-live/pr-l7-multi-turn-integration

### Title
test(memory-v3): multi-turn live-injection integration

### Files
- `assistant/src/memory/v3/__tests__/live-integration.test.ts` (new)
- `assistant/src/memory/v3/__tests__/fixtures/live-turns.json` (new, synthetic)

### Implementation steps
1. Drive a synthetic multi-turn conversation with `memory-v3-live` on (mock the
   provider; reuse the orchestrate/selector mocking patterns):
   - Assert carry-forward: a page pinned in turn 1 appears in turn 2's injected
     `<memory>` block without being re-selected.
   - Assert working-set eviction is reflected in the injected block over turns.
   - Assert exactly one `<memory>` block exists in the assembled context each
     turn (no v2 double-inject).
   - Assert historical user messages have their prior `<memory>` blocks stripped
     each turn (byte-stable history).
2. Use generic synthetic fixtures only (no real content).

### Acceptance criteria
- Multi-turn carry-forward, eviction, single-source, and strip-all behaviors are
  asserted end-to-end.
- Tests pass; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

- **Flipping `memory-v3-live` on for any instance**, A/B, default-on cutover,

- **Companion Terraform flag** in vellum-assistant-platform (recorded in

  *after* the user's text within the same message and anchor on the text block,

## Review: deep-link consumers — Vex APPROVE Reviewed at HEAD `d84b5ef9aba71aa99407e5b3adf63e94fa8b49ab`. CI 11/11 green. Both Codex passes substantively closed across the 3 commits. ### Architecture verification The split into `useGlobalDeepLinkConsumer` (RootLayout) + `useDeepLinkConsumer` (chat domain) + `pending-deep-link-store` (one-shot Zustand inbox) is the right shape — Codex P1's "mount the consumer somewhere always-present" gets the structural fix rather than the easy patch. The store is the narrow-waist hand-off so the global consumer doesn't have to know about `setInput` and the chat-domain consumer doesn't have to know about routing or window activation. Findings closed by construction in the same architecture move: - **Codex P1 (initial, `dbcb1229`)** — consumer only mounted on `ChatPage`, deep links on `/assistant/settings`/`/logs`/etc dropped. Closed at `83f549e8` by lifting nav + window activation to `RootLayout`. - **Devin nit (initial, `dbcb1229`)** — docstring claimed all three handlers fire `ensureMainWindowVisible`. Closed implicitly because the new chat-domain consumer no longer subscribes to the bus directly — its docstring is accurate to its smaller scope. - **Codex P2 (`83f549e8`)** — renderer-side activation can't help when no renderer exists (Darwin keeps the app alive after `window-all-closed`). Closed at `d84b5ef9` by moving the activation into `handleDeepLink` in main, gated on `link.kind !== "unknown"` so foreign schemes can't produce a UI side effect. ### Verified at HEAD - **`handleDeepLink` actually activates the window for actionable kinds** ✓ — `deep-links.ts:140-148`. 4 new tests in `deep-links.test.ts:357-400` pin: `send` activates, `openThread` activates, `unknown`/`javascript:`/`file:`/malformed do NOT activate, and the buffer-then-activate sequence (the actual fix path: link parked AND window recreated). - **Subscribe-then-drain ordering preserved** ✓ — `useEventBusInit`'s drain is async (IPC `invoke`), so React's synchronous effect ordering guarantees `useGlobalDeepLinkConsumer`'s subscribe runs before any drain payload publishes to the bus. The `subscriberCount` model from #32656 still gates correctly: zero → buffer, ≥1 → broadcast-only. - **`useDeepLinkConsumer` doesn't race with `useDraftInput`** ✓ — `useDraftInput` initializes `input` synchronously to `""` and only restores on `isSwitch` (prev key ≠ current key). On initial mount `prevKey === null` → no restore, so an empty composer is the honest state when the pre-fill check runs. On a switch landing simultaneously with a pending message, the second render (input committed to "") re-fires `useDeepLinkConsumer`'s effect via the `composerInput` dep and the pre-fill lands. - **`ensureVisible` is a no-op on already-visible window** ✓ — `main-window.ts:240-250` short-circuits when not destroyed and not minimized. The renderer-side `ensureMainWindowVisible()` duplicating main's call when main triggered creation is harmless. ### Non-blocking observations
1. pending-deep-link-store docstring vs code mismatch on overwrite The docstring at `pending-deep-link-store.ts:13-15` says: > If a second deep link arrives before consumption, the latest message wins (older drops with a Sentry breadcrumb). But `setPendingComposerMessage` is a plain `set({ pendingComposerMessage: message })` with no breadcrumb on overwrite. Either: - Drop the "with a Sentry breadcrumb" clause from the docstring (the silent-overwrite policy is fine — "latest wins" is honest as-is), or - Add a breadcrumb inside the setter when overwriting non-null, mirroring the empty-composer-drop breadcrumb in `useDeepLinkConsumer`. I'd take option 1 — the breadcrumb claim adds an obligation the code doesn't carry, and two-link-overwrite is probably below the noise floor.
2. deeplink.send mid-conversation navigates user away from current thread `useGlobalDeepLinkConsumer` always `navigate(routes.assistant)` on a `send`. If the user is on `/assistant/conversations/` actively typing a reply to that conversation, an external `vellum://send?message=hi` click yanks them to the root chat (their xyz draft is preserved by `useDraftInput` per-conversation, but they lose context). Per the PR body this is intentionally deferred until telemetry — right call. Worth a note for the eventual UX revisit: "open in current conversation" could land the parked message in the active conversation's composer instead of forcing nav. Not blocking — current behavior matches the spec.
3. Main + renderer double-call to ensureMainWindowVisible on the cold path When main triggers window creation (`subscriberCount === 0`, link buffered, `ensureMainWindowVisible()` from `handleDeepLink`), the new renderer mounts, drains the buffered link, publishes it, and `useGlobalDeepLinkConsumer` fires another `ensureMainWindowVisible()` from the renderer. The second call is a no-op, but the doubling is implicit. A short comment at either site noting "main owns the cold path activation (window-all-closed on Darwin), renderer owns the hot path (minimized / behind another window); the duplicate is intentional defense in depth" would save the next reader the trace. Could go on `deep-links.ts:148` or `use-global-deep-link-consumer.ts:42`.
4. Theoretical subscribe-race in preload (already self-flagged) Already called out by the comment in `deep-links.ts:118-122` — a link arriving between renderer's `ipcRenderer.on("vellum:deepLinks:event", handler)` and main processing `vellum:deepLinks:subscribe` could in principle be both buffered and broadcast (delivered twice on next drain). Sub-microsecond window, not realistically triggerable. Renderer-side dedup is the right fix if it ever surfaces; today the comment is the right level of acknowledgment.
### Merge gate - Codex's last pass is at `83f549e899` (pre the `d84b5ef9` main-process activation fix). Devin's only review is at `dbcb1229` (very stale). - The 4 new activation tests pin the Codex P2 closure structurally and CI is 11/11 green at HEAD, so a fresh `@codex review` + `@devin-ai review this PR` at HEAD would formalize closure rather than uncover anything new. Worth firing both before merge per second-approval criterion.

payload.body:
✦ **APPROVE** — reviewed at `4f063cb1`

**Value:** `vellum://` deep links now actually work end-to-end on macOS: cold-start launch opens the window and routes to the right place; hot-path links navigate while the app is running; a click on `/assistant/settings` won't silently drop an inbound `vellum://send`.

<details>
<summary>Full analysis</summary>

## Architecture

Split-hook design is exactly right:

- `useGlobalDeepLinkConsumer` → mounted at `RootLayout` (confirmed in `root-layout.tsx`). Route-stable. Handles navigation + window activation for every authenticated route.
- `useDeepLinkConsumer` → mounted at `ChatPage`. Reads from `usePendingDeepLinkStore` (the narrow-waist hand-off) and pre-fills the composer. Only the chat domain knows about `setInput`; store is how the two halves coordinate across mount timing.

**Codex P1 ("Keep the deep-link consumer mounted outside ChatPage")** is a false positive. Codex saw `useDeepLinkConsumer` in `ChatPage` and missed that `useGlobalDeepLinkConsumer` is already at `RootLayout` doing exactly that job. The split is the architecture.

## deep-links.ts (macOS main)

`subscriberCount → Set<WebContents>`: correct fix. A React effect cleanup that fires before JS context teardown was the only thing preventing `subscriberCount` from leaking — under window-close the renderer process dies before `useEffect` cleanups run, so the counter could stay positive with zero real recipients. Tracking by `WebContents` + auto-deregistering on `destroyed` closes this properly.

`app.isReady()` gate: needed for the cold-start path where `open-url` fires before the app is fully up. Commit title + docs are clear about the timing. Addresses the prior Codex P1.

`ensureVisible as ensureMainWindowVisible` imported from `./main-window` in the main process — correct. The main process handles window activation directly on cold-start without going through the renderer.

## pending-deep-link-store.ts

One-shot semantics, last-write-wins on double-link. Transient (not persisted). All three choices are documented and reasonable. The "two links arriving before consumption" scenario is acknowledged and low-priority.

## runtime/main-window.ts

Clean wrapper: no-ops off Electron, delegates through `window.vellum?.mainWindow.ensureVisible()`. Same shape as `dock.ts` / `app-info.ts` — consistent.

## preload/index.ts

`mainWindow.ensureVisible` added to the bridge. Types updated in `is-electron.ts`. Wired through `ipcMain.handle("vellum:mainWindow:ensureVisible")` in `main-window.ts`. Full chain is solid.

## Tests

- `deep-links.test.ts`: WebContents stub with `fireDestroyed()` — tests the auto-cleanup path. `appIsReady` flag tests the readiness gate. Good coverage.
- `use-deep-link-consumer.test.tsx`: Covers pending-consume, non-empty-composer-drops, whitespace-counts-as-empty.
- `use-global-deep-link-consumer.test.tsx`: Covers send/openThread/unknown event types, window activation call, store parking.
- `main-window.test.ts`: IPC handler registration + routing verified.

## Codex P2 ("Move deep-link window activation out of renderer")

Partially addressed — main process now calls `ensureMainWindowVisible` directly via the `./main-window` import for the cold-start path. The P2 concern about a backgrounded app with closed window is handled: main-process `handleDeepLink` can activate the window without needing a renderer subscriber. The renderer path is defense-in-depth for the hot case. Not blocking.

</details>

*Vellum Constitution — Yours: the assistant responds when you call it — a deep link that silently drops because the user happened to be on settings is the assistant not showing up.*

## Both findings addressed in `83f549e899`

### Codex P1 (consumer only mounted on ChatPage) — closed

Real bug. `vellum://thread/<id>` clicks did nothing on every non-chat route. Fix is the architectural split:

- **`apps/web/src/hooks/use-global-deep-link-consumer.ts`** (new) — mounted at `RootLayout`, alive on every authenticated assistant route. Handles `deeplink.openThread` (navigate to conversation), `deeplink.send` (navigate to `/assistant` + park message in store), `deeplink.unknown` (Sentry breadcrumb). Always fires `ensureMainWindowVisible()` for the navigating handlers.
- **`apps/web/src/stores/pending-deep-link-store.ts`** (new) — Zustand one-shot inbox. Global consumer writes, chat-domain consumer reads-and-clears. Narrow-waist hand-off so the composer pre-fill (which needs `setInput`) stays chat-domain-local without lifting all composer state up.
- **`apps/web/src/domains/chat/hooks/use-deep-link-consumer.ts`** (refactored) — reads `pendingComposerMessage` via the Zustand atomic selector and applies the empty-composer-only policy. No longer subscribes to the bus directly.

Why the hand-off store: the alternative (mount the whole consumer at `RootLayout` and push `setInput` up via outlet context or another Zustand store) would have meant lifting all composer state out of `useDraftInput` — bigger surface than the one-shot store, and `useDraftInput` is intentionally local to its conversation-switch + draft-persistence lifecycle.

### Devin BUG_0001 (docstring inconsistency) — moot post-refactor

Devin flagged the old `useDeepLinkConsumer`'s docstring claiming "all three handlers fire `ensureMainWindowVisible`" but `deeplink.unknown` didn't. The chat-domain hook no longer handles bus events at all post-refactor, and the new global consumer's docstring lists each handler's behavior precisely.

### Tests

9 cases total across the two hooks:
- Global: send navigates + parks + window; openThread navigates + window; unknown breadcrumb-only; unmount unsubscribes.
- Chat-domain: empty-composer pre-fill on pending; non-empty preserves typing + breadcrumb + clears store; whitespace-only empty; no-op when nothing pending; late arrival fires on Zustand re-render.

All green.

Codex P2 (renderer-only activation doesn't help when no renderer exists) addressed in d84b5ef9ab.

The macOS path Codex traced is exact: app alive after main window closes (`window-all-closed` doesn't quit on Darwin), no renderer subscribed, deep link arrives → buffered + broadcast (to zero windows) → never delivered because the renderer-side `ensureMainWindowVisible()` was the only thing that would have recreated the window.

Fix: `handleDeepLink` in main calls `ensureVisible()` from `./main-window` for actionable kinds (`send`, `openThread`), independent of whether a renderer is alive. The renderer then mounts, drains the buffered link, and acts on it. The renderer-side `ensureMainWindowVisible()` stays as defense-in-depth — no-op when the window is already visible.

`unknown` kinds explicitly skip activation: an attacker who could induce the OS to route a `javascript:` URL shouldn't get a UI side effect from us bringing the window forward.

4 new tests pin the behavior:
- `send` + `openThread` each activate the window.
- `unknown` / foreign schemes / malformed URLs do NOT activate.
- The buffer-then-activate sequence (the primary fix path): link is parked AND window recreates so the renderer-on-mount drain delivers it.

30/30 deep-links tests green. Devin BUG_0001 docstring finding remains moot post-`83f549e899` refactor as I noted before.

Two new Codex P1s both addressed in 4f063cb1f2:

**Defer activation until `app.isReady()`** — cold-launch `vellum://` URL fires `open-url` BEFORE `whenReady`. My previous `ensureMainWindowVisible()` call reached `new BrowserWindow()` pre-ready, racing Electron's init. Now gated on `app.isReady()`. Closes the window-close-leak-subscriber bug (renderer JS context torn down before `useEffect` cleanups flush). New test simulates this exact path: subscribe → fire destroyed → next link buffers correctly.

payload.body:
✦ **APPROVE** — reviewed at `bf959ca7ae`

**Value:** Second use of the push-signal bridge pattern from #32651, extended with the new "signals can arrive before the renderer exists" sub-pattern (subscribe-then-drain + main-side buffering). The convention proves out on its first reuse — and the pre-mount buffering layer is exactly the right place to land it, since deep links are the canonical case where the OS hands you a signal before your UI exists.

**What this does:**

- Main: `parseVellumUrl` (pure, exhaustive over send/openThread/unknown), `extractDeepLinkFromArgv` (Windows/Linux second-instance), `installDeepLinks` wires both schemes + `will-finish-launching → open-url` (the launching-URL trap) + `second-instance` + `vellum:deepLinks:drain` IPC + new `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` IPC channels.
- Bridge: `window.vellum.deepLinks.drain()` + `onLink(cb)` with subscribe/unsubscribe IPC sent inside the callback lifecycle.
- Renderer: `subscribeToDeepLinks` + `drainPendingDeepLinks` runtime wrappers (no-op off Electron), three new `BusEventMap` entries (`deeplink.send` / `deeplink.openThread` / `deeplink.unknown`), `use-event-bus-init` subscribes first then drains.
- Docs: `ELECTRON.md` gains the "signals before renderer exists" sub-section; `EVENT_BUS.md` event table extended.

<details>
<summary>Full analysis</summary>

### Codex P2 (live-link replay on renderer reload) — closed at `fbdc7bef51`, refined at `bf959ca7ae`

The original `drained: boolean` flag closed the replay case but introduced the logout-relogin gap that your audit caught. The pivot to **subscriber-counted buffering** is the right shape — it stops conflating "has drained" with "is subscribed now":

```ts
if (subscriberCount === 0) pending.push(link);
broadcast(link);
```

This closes both cases by construction:
- **Renderer reload, subscriber present:** count > 0 → broadcast-only → drain returns nothing the second time.
- **Logout, no subscriber:** count === 0 → buffered → next renderer drains it.

Test coverage matches the intent: "with a subscriber present, live links broadcast but do NOT enter the buffer (no replay on renderer reload)" + "logout-relogin: link arriving while unsubscribed lands in the buffer for the next subscriber" + the clamp-to-zero accounting test. The pairing of test names to failure modes is exemplary — anyone reading the test list sees the model.

### Residual race — documented + accepted

The inline comment on `subscriberCount` calls out the sub-microsecond window between renderer's `ipcRenderer.on` and main's processing of the `subscribe` IPC. Acknowledging it inline is the right call — it's not realistically triggerable by user action (deep links arrive on user click, not at IPC-roundtrip frequency), but the comment prevents the next reader from "fixing" it with a more complex design.

### Subscribe-then-drain ordering

`use-event-bus-init.ts:lines ~150–165` does the subscribe-first, drain-second sequence. Verified the comment explanation matches the implementation — the inline note about "any in-flight link is delivered via `onLink` and the drained buffer carries the pre-renderer-ready backlog" is correct as long as the main-side buffer is subscriber-counted (which it is at HEAD).

### Pattern extension — `ELECTRON.md`

The new sub-section codifies the rule: bridges where the signal can arrive pre-mount need both a `subscribe<X>` (live) and a `drainPending<X>` (backlog) surface, and consumers must subscribe-then-drain. This is the kind of documentation that prevents the next contributor from rediscovering the race by hand. High-leverage.

### Observations (non-blocking)

1. **Renderer crash / freeze leaks subscriberCount.** If a `webContents` crashes without the preload cleanup running (which is the cleanup path for `subscribe → unsubscribe` IPC), the count stays incremented. Subsequent links arrive with count > 0 → broadcast-only → lost (no live consumer to receive them). A more robust shape: track `subscribers: Set<WebContents>` on the first `subscribe` IPC from each sender and listen for `webContents.on("destroyed")` to clean up. Same semantics for the common path; survives crashes. Doesn't need to land in this PR — it's a refinement of a residual edge case, not a correctness gap on the common path.

2. **Unhandled rejection in `drainPendingDeepLinks().then(...)`.** The `.then` has no `.catch`. If `publishDeepLink` (or `bus.publish` downstream) throws, the rejection is silent. The `appStateChange` import in the same effect has a `Sentry.captureException` `.catch` — worth mirroring here for parity:

   ```ts
   void drainPendingDeepLinks()
     .then((pending) => { for (const link of pending) publishDeepLink(link); })
     .catch((err) => Sentry.captureException(err, { level: "warning", tags: { context: "deep_link_drain" } }));
   ```

3. **`use-event-bus-init.ts` size.** Confirming your own audit-comment flag — at ~290 lines and growing one effect-branch per source, the "one helper per signal source" refactor is overdue. Right call to leave it out of this PR. When you do it, the test file colocation should follow the same split (today it's one mega-file).

### Merge gate

- CI 11/11 green at HEAD
- Codex review at HEAD: no comments (P2 closed in code)
- Devin review: 0 potential issues
- 26 deep-links tests + 5 bus-init tests covering both replay + logout-relogin regressions

Mergeable.

</details>

*Vellum Constitution — Conventions pay off on reuse: the push-signal bridge pattern from #32651 ports cleanly to deep links and extends to the pre-renderer case without bending. The subscriber-counted buffering refinement is the kind of audit-driven correction that turns a working fix into a structurally correct one.*

payload.author: ashleeradka
payload.body:
## Audit-found bug + fix — `drained` flag was wrong shape

Pushed `bf959ca7ae`. The previous "drained-once means live-only-mode-forever" approach addressed the Codex P2 replay case but introduced a new bug: links arriving while NO renderer is subscribed (logout, between hard navigates) would be neither buffered nor delivered.

**Trace of the bug:**
1. User logged out, clicks `vellum://send?message=hello` → buffered. ✓
2. User logs in → drain returns it. `drained = true` forever. ✓
3. User logs out → renderer unmounts.
4. User clicks `vellum://thread/abc` → broadcast hits zero listeners, `drained === true` so no buffer → **link lost**.
5. User logs back in → drain returns `[]`. Thread never opens.

The flag conflated "has ever drained" with "is subscribed right now."

**Fix: explicit subscriber tracking via two new IPC channels.**

- `vellum:deepLinks:subscribe` — preload sends on `onLink` registration. Main increments `subscriberCount`.
- `vellum:deepLinks:unsubscribe` — preload sends on cleanup. Main decrements (clamped to 0).

`handleDeepLink` buffers iff `subscriberCount === 0`. `drain` always returns + clears; no more permanent flag.

This closes:
- **Codex P2** (live-link replay on renderer reload) — still closed because live links with a subscriber present don't enter the buffer.
- **Logout-relogin lost-link case** — newly closed because the buffer fills again when the subscriber count drops to 0.

Residual race documented inline: a link arriving in the sub-microsecond window between renderer's `ipcRenderer.on` registration and main's processing of the subscribe IPC could be double-delivered. Not realistically triggerable.

26/26 deep-links tests + 34/34 bus-init tests green at HEAD.

## Audit checklist — other items reviewed

- **Location**, **abstraction shape**, **DRY** (bridge-type duplication is the documented convention): clean.
- **`use-event-bus-init.ts` approaching ~290 lines.** Each new signal source has grown Effect 1. Worth a "split each source into its own publish helper" refactor — **not in this PR** to keep it focused. Flagging here so the next contributor knows the limit is approaching.
- **No internal-tracker refs**, **no barrel files**, **tests colocated**, **no cross-domain imports**, **file size under 300**: clean.
- **Documentation**: ELECTRON.md gained the "signals before renderer exists" sub-section; EVENT_BUS.md table extended with the three `deeplink.*` rows.
