payload.body:
✦ **APPROVE** — reviewed at `25a2dcbd4e`

**Value:** Closes the architectural finish line #32641's PR description pointed at. The action-registry pattern, NOOP defaults, render-time capture race, and selector-flip race — all four Codex P1s from #32641 dissolve because the state machine no longer lives inside React's render-and-effect timing. Plus: the machine is now directly testable without `renderHook`.

**What this does:**

- New `lifecycle-service.ts` (642 lines) — module-level singleton class owning state machine, watchdog, retry budgets, generation counter, gateway-auth short-circuit, cache seeding, onboarding-redirect coordination.
- `use-lifecycle.ts` shrinks 676 → 99 lines — pure wiring: pull React signals + push via `setInputs`, hand poll results via `applyServerResult`. No state, no callbacks.
- `lifecycle-store.ts` shrinks 110 → 39 lines — `assistantState` only. The store is now strictly an observability surface; only the service writes.
- Consumer call shape simplifies: `useAssistantLifecycleStore.getState().checkAssistant()` → `lifecycleService.checkAssistant()` across `chat-page`, `hatching-screen`, `pre-chat-flow`, `use-event-bus-init`.
- New direct unit tests in `lifecycle-service.test.ts` exercise server-state projection (active + self-hosted), the auto-hatch cascade (nonprod / retired / vanilla-managed branches), the logout reset, and the gateway-auth short-circuit. No `renderHook`, no React tree.

<details>
<summary>Full analysis</summary>

### Codex P1 (watchdog reset on every poll) — closed at `4a9aade767`

The original `transition()` cleared+re-armed the watchdog on every call, so back-to-back `initializing → initializing` poll results reset the 5-minute clock indefinitely and `recoverStuckInitializingAssistant()` could never fire on a genuinely stuck hatch. Fix is edge-triggered:

```ts
if (next.kind !== "initializing") {
  if (this.initializingTimeout) clearTimeout(...);
} else if (prevKind !== "initializing") {
  this.armInitializingWatchdog();
}
```

A repeat `initializing → initializing` is a no-op kind-wise — no clear, no re-arm. `hatchAndCheck()` calls `armInitializingWatchdog()` explicitly so a fresh hatch attempt still resets the clock. The inline comment spells out the invariant — high-leverage for the next maintainer.

### Codex P2 (pre-mount lifecycle call → null queryClient) — closed at `26521f2162`

`ready: boolean` ships false, `setInputs()` is the only flip-to-true. Every public action (`checkAssistant`, `respondToInputs`, `applyServerResult`) early-returns `if (!this.ready)`. So a child route whose `useEffect` commits before `RootLayout`'s `setInputs` lands — the parent/child effect commit-order race — becomes a silent no-op instead of TypeError-on-`null.fetchQuery` followed by a spurious `network-error` state being published.

This is the structural equivalent of the `NOOP_CHECK` defaults the previous version shipped — same invariant, but the guard lives once on the class instead of being scattered across three action fields with NOOP fallbacks the store had to expose. The docstring on `ready` explicitly cites the race; future maintainers see why it's there.

### Test architecture

Bun's `mock.module` at module scope + `lifecycleService.__resetForTesting()` in `beforeEach/afterEach` is the right pattern for a module-level singleton. The comment in `beforeEach` about why `mockClear` isn't enough (and why every new mock needs a fresh baseline) is doing real work — the kind of subtle leak that costs 30 minutes of debugging a flaky test.

The fact that auto-hatch cascade, retry-budget exhaustion, and the gateway-auth short-circuit are now reachable from a unit test — no `renderHook`, no fake timers, no time-travel reasoning about effect commit order — is the headline benefit of the extraction. The state machine being a class with `__resetForTesting` is the kind of testability boring frontend code rarely gets.

### Observations (non-blocking)

1. **`useEffect` dep array in `use-lifecycle.ts:75–86`** lists `onRedirect` and `resolveOnboardingRedirect`. If the parent constructs either inline per render, the effect re-runs every render → `setInputs` re-publishes identical values → `respondToInputs` re-fires. Most calls are early-return no-ops inside the service, so it's not a correctness bug — but worth confirming `RootLayout` wraps both in `useCallback`. The kind of thing the next render-perf pass will catch if it's drifted.

2. **`getLocalGatewayUrl` mock at `lifecycle-service.test.ts:41`** is set up but I don't see it asserted in any test. Either dead mock or pending coverage for the local-gateway projection path. Drop it or add the assertion.

3. **`useCallback` wrappers in `chat-page.tsx:174–187`** — still necessary because `lifecycleService.checkAssistant` is a normal class method (passing the bare reference loses `this`). Two cleaner shapes if you ever want to revisit: (a) define the actions as arrow-class-fields so `this` binds at construction; (b) ship pre-bound exports next to the singleton. Current form is fine — the comment above each wrapper could shrink now that the identity-flip rationale is gone, but not worth a follow-up commit.

### Merge gate

- CI 7/7 green at HEAD
- Codex review at HEAD: "Didn't find any major issues. Hooray!"
- Devin review: 0 potential issues
- Both Codex inline findings (P1 watchdog, P2 input guard) verified closed in code

Mergeable.

</details>

*Vellum Constitution — Trust-seeking: by lifting the state machine out of React's commit-order choreography, the four classes of failure modes Codex caught in the predecessor PR become structurally impossible to express, and the machine is now reachable from unit tests with no time-travel reasoning about render order.*

payload.body:
✦ **Re-APPROVE** — reviewed at `c9a8b15da0`

Two commits since the prior APPROVE at `25a2dcbd4e`, both targeted at observations from that review.

**Test coverage extension (`c9a8b15da0`, closing LUM-2067):**

12 direct unit tests now, +2 from the prior pass — both exercising the recovery code that was the last meaningful uncovered area in the service:

1. **Watchdog → retire → re-hatch end-to-end.** The watchdog is reachable from a test only because `transition()`'s edge-trigger fix (`4a9aade767`) stopped `initializing → initializing` poll repeats from indefinitely resetting the clock. The test captures that explicitly: a `getAssistant → initializing` projection arms the watchdog, the watchdog fires after `TEST_INITIALIZING_TIMEOUT_MS` (30ms), `retireAssistantById` is called with the captured `initializingAssistantId`, then `hatchAssistant` follows up. The structural fix made the test possible — which is exactly the right shape.

2. **`MAX_INITIALIZING_RECOVERIES` budget.** Drives four watchdog cycles where each recovery's re-hatch returns initializing (the assistant stays stuck). After the budget exhausts, the next firing transitions to `buildInitializingTimeoutError`. The kind of off-by-one that would surface as users *permanently stuck* on the initializing screen — now a regression test catches it.

**The mocking pattern is the right call.** `mock.module("@/assistant/lifecycle", ...)` overrides only `INITIALIZING_TIMEOUT_MS`, preserving the real `resolveAssistantLifecycleState` / `buildInitializingTimeoutError` / `shouldRecoverFromHatchFailure` helpers. The state machine alone can't reach those outcomes without a poll driver, so `onboarding-lifecycle-sync.test.tsx` carries them. That's a principled unit-vs-integration boundary, not a coverage gap to apologize for.

**Comment cleanup (`ad191fd7b9`):**

payload.author: vex-assistant-bot
payload.body:
Reviewed HEAD `a00dc62ae5` (4 commits, +177/-182, 13 files). CI green: `Lint, Type Check & Build` + `Type Check` + `Build` + `Test` + `Lint` + Socket Security ×2 all success. The right cut for Part D — net **deletion** PR (-5 lines) via boilerplate removal + DRY win + dead-code removal, with all bot findings closing by construction across the 3 fix commits.

**Adoption verification — 7 routed files**
- `skills-tab.tsx` ✓ `getLocalBool(TIP_STORAGE_KEY, false)` (was raw `=== "1"` with SSR guard)
- `mic-permission-primer.tsx` ✓ `getLocalBool(MIC_PRIMER_STORAGE_KEY, false)` (was try/catch + `!== "true"`)
- `chat-route-content.tsx` ✓ `getLocalBool` / `setLocalBool` / `removeLocalSetting`
- `chat-layout.tsx` ✓ 4-helper mix: `getLocalBool/setLocalBool` (sidebar collapsed) + `getLocalNumber/setLocalNumber` (sidebar width). Was raw + try/catch + manual `Number()` parsing.
- `impersonate-version-flag.ts` ✓ `getLocalSetting` / `setLocalSetting` / `removeLocalSetting` + verify-after-write
- `use-draft-input.ts` ✓ `getLocalSetting` / `setLocalSetting`
- `use-push-to-talk.ts` ✓ `getLocalSetting` with explicit off-default on empty

**Files correctly kept inline** (sanity-checked via grep against full `apps/web/src/**/*.ts*`):
- `current-platform-assistant-store.ts` — implements Zustand `persist` `StateStorage` adapter (literally needs raw access)
- `client-feature-flag-store.ts` — iterates dynamic `LS_PREFIX + key` set; the null-vs-absent distinction matters
- `gateway-session.ts` — auth infrastructure with `LS_TOKEN_KEY ?? LEGACY_TOKEN_KEY` multi-key coordination
- `device-settings.ts` — typed registry with its own `entry.key ?? entry.legacy` migration fallbacks
- `oauth-popup-complete-page.tsx` / `oauth-complete-page.tsx` / `google-connect-screen.tsx` / `integration-detail-modal.tsx` (3 remaining) — cross-tab IPC via `StorageEvent`, not traditional storage
- `local-settings.ts` / `typed-storage.ts` — base layer
- `storage-migration.ts` / `session-cleanup.ts` / `sandbox-bridge.ts` — migration/cleanup infrastructure that needs raw access
- All grep'd; PR body's justification table covers each.

**Bonus wins beyond stated scope**
1. **OAuth utility DRY (-60 lines)**: `integration-detail-modal.tsx` had a full copy of `OAuthCompletePayload`, `oauthCompletionStorageKey`, `getOAuthCompleteMessagePayload`, `getOAuthCompleteStoragePayload` from `lib/auth/oauth-popup.ts`. Now imported from canonical source (verified at L43-47). The 5 call sites (L271/287/339/514/518) all use the imported names.
2. **Nudge legacy cleanup relocation (-26 lines from `nudge-store.ts`)**: Moved from `nudge-store.ts` (where it ran inside the store module on first import) to `storage-migration.ts` via 6 `removeKey()` calls + the `app.nudgeLegacy.cleaned` flag itself. **Two architectural wins from the move**: (a) the `app.nudgeLegacy.cleaned` flag becomes unnecessary because `removeKey()` is idempotent (removeItem on absent key is a no-op); (b) cleanup is now co-located with all other one-time storage migrations, single import-time execution point.

**Bot findings — all 5 closed at HEAD**

| # | Bot | Finding | Closed in |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Codex P2 | Mic primer shown on storage failure (was hidden) | Documented as intentional in PR body — consent-transparency > silent suppression, Devin defended in thread |
| 2 | Devin BUG_0001 | Skills tip dismissed-flag lost ("1" vs "true" format mismatch) | `6086c39` — new `migrateValue(key, oldValue, newValue)` helper + `migrateValue("vellum:skills:tipDismissed", "1", "true")` in `runStorageMigrations()`. Idempotent (only writes when current matches `oldValue`). Migration order verified correct: `migrateKey("vellum:skillsTabTipDismissed", "vellum:skills:tipDismissed")` runs first (line 129), then `migrateValue("vellum:skills:tipDismissed", "1", "true")` (line 176) — handles both renamed-but-old-format AND already-renamed-new-format users. |
| 3 | Devin BUG_0002 | PTT silently activates with Ctrl when storage fails | `6086c39` — `raw ? parseActivator(raw) : { kind: "off" }` at L122-124. See observation #2 below — this also changes first-time-user default behavior; worth a thought. |
| 4 | Codex P2 | Impersonate flag reloads even when storage write fails | `fe5c5d8` — `getImpersonatedAssistantVersion()` re-read after `setLocalSetting`/`removeLocalSetting`. If mismatch, log warn + return early without reload. Both branches (set / clear) handled symmetrically. |
| 5 | Codex P2 | `"app."` prefix in `LEGACY_USER_PREFIXES` sweeps active iOS/macOS nudge keys | `a00dc62` — removed `"app."` entirely from `LEGACY_USER_PREFIXES` (8 entries remain: `onboarding., voice:, gw:, ff:client:, local:, integrations., vellumDebug., vellum_`). Dead `app.githubNudge.*` + `app.discordNudge.*` + `app.nudgeLegacy.cleaned` keys removed at startup via explicit `removeKey()` calls in `storage-migration.ts:181-187`, not at logout. New test `"preserves active app. nudge keys on logout"` asserts `app.iosNudge.downloaded`, `app.macOsNudge.bannerDismissed`, AND `app.githubNudge.starred` all survive `clearUserScopedStorage()`. |

Codex's last pass at `fe5c5d8e81` predates `a00dc62ae5` — the `app.` finding is closed at HEAD; one `@codex review` ping would formalize closure. Devin Review surface mentions 5 additional findings — 30-second look at app.devin.ai/review/.../pull/32652 before merge.

**Migration correctness audit** (cross-checked against logout-auth-review.md checklist)
- ✓ Navigation: unchanged (logout path is upstream)
- ✓ User-scope sweep: `vellum:` prefix + 8 legacy prefixes correct; `LEGACY_DEVICE_KEYS` Set (9 entries) correctly excludes device-scoped legacy keys (`vellum_theme`, `vellum_share_analytics`, etc., plus `onboarding.lastUserId` which matches `"onboarding."` prefix but is device-scoped)
- ✓ sessionStorage: fully cleared at top of `clearUserScopedStorage()`
- ✓ BYOK credentials: `vellum:ai:geminiKey/perplexityKey/braveKey/tavilyKey` correctly clear via `vellum:` prefix sweep
- ✓ Device keys: preserved via Set exclusion in `isUserScopedKey()`
- ✓ Active nudge keys (`app.iosNudge.*`, `app.macOsNudge.*`): preserved (no longer swept)
- ✓ Dead nudge keys (`app.githubNudge.*`, `app.discordNudge.*`, `app.nudgeLegacy.cleaned`): removed at startup, idempotent (next launch is no-op)
- ✓ Verify-after-write on impersonate: matches old catch-block early-return semantics
- ✓ Tests: 47 pass (37 migration + 10 cleanup). New tests: `migrateValue` (3 unit) + skills tip integration (1) + nudge cleanup (1) + app. preservation (1)

**Non-blocking observations**

1. **PR body framing of mic-primer change is the right call.** Showing the consent flow when storage is broken is correct UX — a permission dialog requires user understanding, and silently suppressing the explanation while still triggering the OS prompt is worse. The intentional-change framing is honest and the Devin defense in-thread is convincing. Good behavioral-change disclosure pattern; this is the shape future PRs that make storage-failure semantics changes should follow.

2. **PTT first-time-user default also changed, not just the storage-failure case.** The fix `raw ? parseActivator(raw) : { kind: "off" }` treats empty `raw` as `"off"`. But `getLocalSetting(key, "")` returns `""` in *both* scenarios: (a) storage failure, (b) key not present (first-time user). The old code called `parseActivator(localStorage.getItem(key))` which for `null` returns `{ kind: "modifierOnly", modifiers: ["control"] }` — so the OLD first-time-user default was PTT-active-on-Ctrl, and the NEW first-time-user default is PTT-off. Devin's review (and the fix) frames PTT-Ctrl-on-storage-failure as a bug, which I agree with — surprise voice recording on Ctrl is bad UX. But the same change also removes Ctrl-PTT as the first-time-user default. If that default was intentional (Ctrl is a common PTT activator across apps), this is a minor regression for new users. If it was just a side effect of `parseActivator(null)` semantics, the change is correct. Worth a one-line PR-body note like the mic-primer one to document the intent. Not blocking.

3. **Test description `"preserves active app. nudge keys on logout"` includes `app.githubNudge.starred`** (dead key). The assertion is correct from logout's perspective (logout doesn't touch any `app.*` keys after the prefix removal), but the description groups dead and active keys together. A comment in the test body distinguishes them, but the test name could read as "github nudge is active" to a future reader. Cosmetic.

4. **No test for the impersonate verify-after-write pattern.** The fix is correct (verified by tracing) but `setImpersonatedAssistantVersion` is a debug surface — it's reasonable to skip. A unit test with `MemoryStorage` that throws on `setItem` would lock in the no-reload-on-failure invariant. Minor.

**LUM-2042 arc completeness**
- PR A (#32604, LUM-2044, typed-storage factory) ✓ merged
- PR B (#32621, LUM-2045, key naming standardization) ✓ merged
- PR C (#32645, LUM-2046, domain storage migration) ✓ merged
- PR D (this one, LUM-2047, route inline calls) — this approval closes the arc

Four-PR sequencing was the right shape: factory → keys → high-traffic domain stores → leaf consumers. Each PR independently reviewable, no Big Bang merge. Per the carry-forward from #32645, every callsite migration to the snapshot-caching accessor was audited for `load*().push/splice/sort/assign`-style mutation; this PR's adoption is all imperative get/set helpers (not snapshot accessors), so the mutation-leak class doesn't apply here.

**Merge gate**: CI green at HEAD. All 5 bot findings substantively closed. Codex's last pass (`fe5c5d8e81`) predates the `app.` removal in `a00dc62`. Fresh `@codex review` + `@devin-ai review this PR` at HEAD would formalize closure.

payload.author: vex-assistant-bot
payload.body:
Reviewed HEAD `61099b7c4b` (4 commits, 11 files +621/-18). CI 11/11 green. Codex re-review at HEAD already cleared ("Didn't find any major issues. Already looking forward to the next diff."). The right architectural cut — this is the convention-setting PR for every future push-signal bridge.

**Architecture verification — 6-layer flow**

1. **`apps/macos/src/main/power-events.ts`** (87 lines): subscribes to all 5 powerMonitor events (`suspend`, `resume`, `lock-screen`, `unlock-screen`, `user-did-become-active`), per-kind 1s debounce against macOS's historical duplicate-delivery behavior, broadcast via `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()` with `isDestroyed()` skip, idempotent install via module-scope `installed` flag, `before-quit` clears debounce timestamps so dev hot-reload re-arms from zero. `__resetForTesting` is the right test seam (named for what it is, no production reachability).
2. **`apps/macos/src/main/index.ts`**: `installPowerEvents()` called once at line 254 — verified single install site.
3. **`apps/macos/src/preload/index.ts`**: `window.vellum.power.onEvent(callback) → unsubscribe`. `PowerEventKind` + `PowerEvent` inlined for the same reason as `VellumCommand` / `AppVersionInfo` (cheaper to maintain a tiny literal union three places than wire cross-project TS imports; drift surfaces as a renderer handler not narrowing on a new kind = graceful no-op, not a crash). Returns the unsubscribe closure correctly.
4. **`apps/web/src/runtime/is-electron.ts`**: ambient `power: { onEvent(...) }` field mirrored.
5. **`apps/web/src/runtime/power-events.ts`** (40 lines): no-op-off-Electron wrapper, returns unsubscribe-noop, optional-chains `window.vellum?.power.onEvent` for safety. Matches the shape of `dock.ts` / `app-info.ts`.
6. **`apps/web/src/stores/event-bus-store.ts`**: `BusEventMap` grows `power.suspend/resume/lock/unlock/active` with `Record<string, never>` payload (correct — no payload needed, the discriminator is the event name).
7. **`apps/web/src/hooks/use-event-bus-init.ts`**: Effect 1 fans `PowerEvent` into bus events via single subscribe + switch; Effect 2 wires the SSE handlers.

**The convention extension is exactly the right rule.** ELECTRON.md gains 16 lines documenting "cross-domain push signals route through the event bus, not directly via the bridge" — clean separation between imperative wrappers (`setDockBadge`, `getAppVersionInfo`) and push-signal wrappers (publishes into bus, consumers subscribe via bus). This pays compounding interest: future deep-link bridge, notification-action bridge, global-hotkey bridge all follow the same 5-step shape, and domain consumers stay platform-agnostic — the same `bus.subscribe("power.resume", ...)` works whether the source was `powerMonitor` (Electron), `visibilitychange` (web), or Capacitor `appStateChange` (iOS).

**Bot findings — all closed by construction, not patched**

1. **Codex P1 (54997aff93) + Devin BUG_0001 (61099b7c4b)** — same finding: `power.resume` / `power.unlock` reuse `handleResume` which has `if (current) return`, so in the tray-resident case (renderer never went hidden) the handler no-ops on the exact bug it exists to fix. Closed in `d9985623b1` by **splitting into two handlers** with different semantics: `handleAppResume` (renderer visibility) keeps the open-if-null behavior, `handlePowerResume` (system-level) bounces unconditionally (teardown + open). Right shape — the underlying semantic distinction (visibility vs power) is real, not a flag on a shared handler. Two new tests pin the tray-resident path with no preceding `app.hidden`.

2. **Devin ANALYSIS_0004** — no `power.suspend` handler for SSE teardown. Closed in `661c2d4c0d`: `bus.subscribe("power.suspend", teardownIfOpen)` mirrors the `app.hidden` teardown. PR body's reasoning is correct — clean daemon disconnect beats waiting for TCP timeouts, and the bounce-on-resume path stays as defense-in-depth in case the suspend event drops (Electron's documented macOS behavior, also why the main-side debounce exists).

3. **Self-caught audit finding (61099b7c4b)** — shared dedup window `lastResumeAt` was wrong. Trace: tray-resident wake → wifi reconnects → `online` → `app.resume(signal:"online")` → `handleAppResume` updates `lastResumeAt`, no-ops on non-null current → 50ms later `power.resume` arrives → suppressed by shared dedup → half-dead SSE persists. The exact case the PR exists to fix. Split into `lastAppResumeAt` + `lastPowerActionAt` so handlers don't observe each other's timestamps; each self-dedups against its own action's recency. Two new tests pin the bug (`app.resume no-op (current non-null) does NOT suppress a follow-up power.resume bounce`) AND the acceptable tradeoff (`app.resume then power.resume — fresh SSE gets bounced (wasted bounce, but the correctness tradeoff)`). The tradeoff doc in the comment is the right framing: <100ms wasted bounce in the rare hidden-AND-power-signal case is acceptable to close the missed-bounce bug in the common tray-resident case.

**Test coverage at HEAD**
- `power-events.test.ts` (macos, 7 cases): 5-event subscription, idempotent install, broadcast to every window, skip destroyed, electron-name → bus-kind mapping, 1s per-kind debounce, no cross-kind debouncing.
- `use-event-bus-init.test.tsx` (+8 new cases): power.suspend tears down live SSE; power.suspend no-op when no SSE; power.resume bounces LIVE SSE (tray-resident); power.unlock bounces live SSE; power.resume reopens after teardown; power.unlock reopens after teardown; app.resume no-op doesn't suppress power.resume (the audit-fix bug); app.resume + power.resume = 2 bounces (the tradeoff).
- Manual checklist (unchecked in PR body): close lid 10min + reopen; lock screen + unlock. These are the ones that exercise the real powerMonitor — worth doing before merge.

**Anti-pattern audit clean**
- ✓ `subscribeToPowerEvents` returns the unsubscribe closure; Effect 1 cleanup calls it (`unsubPower()` at the cleanup return). No leak on hook unmount or hot-reload.
- ✓ `window.vellum?.power.onEvent` optional-chains the bridge field — safe if the preload hasn't initialized yet.
- ✓ Effect 1 (lifecycle) and Effect 2 (SSE) are separate `useEffect` blocks. Power subscription mounts before the first power event can fire (React 18 batches effects in commit phase, Effect 1 runs first in declaration order); Effect 2's bus subscriptions are registered before any power event arrives in steady state.
- ✓ Bus subscriptions in Effect 2 are correctly cleaned up — 6 `unsub*()` calls at the cleanup return.
- ✓ Main-side broadcast skips `isDestroyed()` windows (prevents IPC channel-disconnected errors after window destruction).
- ✓ Per-kind debounce uses a `Partial<Record<PowerEventKind, number>>` — narrow types throughout.
- ✓ `before-quit` cleanup of debounce timestamps prevents stale state in dev hot-reload.
- ✓ `Record<string, never>` payload type on bus events is correct for empty-payload events (vs `{}` which TS allows arbitrary fields on).

**Non-blocking observations**

1. **About-window double-fire.** The About window is also a `BrowserWindow`, so it receives every power broadcast via `getAllWindows()`. Its preload doesn't subscribe today, so the renderer never registers an IPC listener for `vellum:power:event`, and Electron silently drops the message. Quiet by design — no log spam, no leak. But every future auxiliary window (Settings, Help) gets the same behavior by default, which is correct. Worth noting in the PR body's "broadcast model" paragraph (already there in the main-side file's docstring) so future bridge authors don't try to add their own per-window targeting.

2. **`PowerEvent` payload is `{ kind }` only.** Future-proofing thought: if any consumer needs the system-side timestamp (e.g. "how long were we asleep"), it can't reconstruct it from the renderer-side `Date.now()` because the IPC message is debounced at the main side. Not a blocker today — the SSE bounce semantics don't need duration — but a `{ kind, at: number }` shape would be a tiny addition if a future consumer needs it. Skip unless needed.

3. **`lastAppResumeAt` / `lastPowerActionAt` shared across all power events.** `power.unlock` and `power.resume` share `lastPowerActionAt`, so unlocking the screen within 1s of waking the system collapses to one bounce — that's the desired behavior. But `power.lock` and `power.active` (which don't have a handler today) also fall in the `power.*` family conceptually; if a future consumer wires them to bounce-on-something, they'd want a separate dedup window. The current shape "one dedup window per handler closure" is correct as long as new handlers create their own; just worth a one-line comment in the docstring so future readers don't reuse `lastPowerActionAt` for an unrelated handler.

4. **`subscribeToPowerEvents` returns `() => undefined` — `() => void` would be cleaner.** Minor TS style nit; `void` vs `undefined` return is interchangeable in practice but the type signature uses `() => void`, and an arrow returning `undefined` works but reads weird. `() => {}` or `() => {return;}` would match. Cosmetic.

Codex P1 (power.resume no-ops on live SSE — the central case the PR was supposed to fix) addressed in d9985623b1.

The fix is two handlers sharing the dedup window but with different semantics:

- **`handleAppResume`** (`app.resume`): renderer became visible. Reopen only if no current connection — the connection was either never torn down or just opened.
- **`handlePowerResume`** (`power.resume`, `power.unlock`): system-level resume. Bounce **unconditionally** — teardown + open — because the socket may be half-dead from sleep regardless of renderer visibility.

Shared dedup window: a sleep that ALSO triggered a visibility change doesn't double-bounce; whichever signal arrives first wins.

Two tests added for the central case:
- `power.resume` bounces a LIVE SSE (no preceding `app.hidden`) — the tray-resident case the PR exists to fix.
- `power.unlock` bounces a LIVE SSE — same shape for screen unlock.

## Audit-driven follow-up — one real bug + one doc gap, both addressed in 61099b7c4b

### Real bug: shared dedup window let `app.resume`'s no-op suppress a needed `power.resume` bounce

Trace the tray-resident wake path more carefully than my earlier commit did:

1. System sleeps 5 min. Renderer stays visible (tray-resident / full-screen, no `app.hidden`).
2. On wake, wifi reconnects ~200ms later → `online` event → bus publishes `app.resume(signal: "online")`.
3. `handleAppResume` runs: dedup check passes (first fire), **updates the shared `lastResumeAt`**, calls `checkAssistant`, sees `current` is non-null (we never went hidden), returns without action.
4. ~50ms later `power.resume` reaches `handlePowerResume`.
5. `handlePowerResume` checks `lastResumeAt` — recent — deduped, returns **without bouncing**.
6. Half-dead SSE persists. This is the exact case the PR exists to fix.

**Fix**: split into `lastAppResumeAt` + `lastPowerActionAt`. The two handlers don't observe each other's timestamps; each self-dedups against its own action's recency.

**Tradeoff** (called out in a renamed test): the rare case where the renderer both went hidden AND received a system-power signal on wake now wastes one extra bounce — `app.resume` opens a fresh SSE, `power.resume` immediately bounces it. <100ms, no user-visible regression. Acceptable cost for closing the missed-bounce bug in the much more common tray-resident case.

### Doc gap: `EVENT_BUS.md` event-protocol table didn't include `power.*`

Added all five entries with bus-owned action + the future-ticket note for `power.lock` / `power.active` (no consumer today).

### Tests

- **New**: `app.resume` no-op (current non-null) does NOT suppress a follow-up `power.resume` bounce. The regression case.
- **Updated**: "app.resume then power.resume" — the old assertion documented the (buggy) shared-dedup behavior; the new assertion documents the independent-dedup behavior + the wasted-bounce tradeoff explicitly.

28/28 bus-init tests green.

### Audit checklist coverage

Other items reviewed and clean: file location, runtime-wrapper shape (matches `dock.ts` / `app-info.ts`), IPC channel-per-family discriminator (matches PATTERNS.md), three-file bridge convention (per ELECTRON.md), Zustand integration, no barrel files, no internal-tracker refs. File size on `use-event-bus-init.ts` is approaching the ~300-line threshold but Effect 1 (sources) and Effect 2 (SSE policy) are still coherent — a "sources" / "SSE-policy" split is a separate refactor PR if it ever becomes useful.

Reviewed HEAD `238b1bf1bc`. 7/7 CI green (incl. type check passing after Devin's upstream-merge fixup at `238b1bf1bc`). Clean extraction; factory pattern matches codebase convention; type colocation cleanup is a real win.

**Behavioral preservation verified**
- Watchdog encapsulates timer + per-attempt counters + Sentry telemetry. `arm/clear/resetCounters/recordTraffic/consumeLastAbortCause` is the exact surface the transport needs — no leaky internals.
- Per-attempt `AbortController` retained; watchdog targets the active controller via `arm(controller, attempt)`, so a stall on attempt N doesn't poison attempt N+1.
- `lastAbortCause` set only inside the timer callback (`"watchdog"`); reconnect path reads via `consumeLastAbortCause() ?? "error"`. Single producer, single consumer per attempt, cleared on read — correct.
- Watchdog armed AFTER `onReconnect` resolves (HTTP reconcile is multi-second; arming earlier would charge that against `idleTimeoutMs`). Comment captures the reasoning.
- `finally { watchdog.clear() }` around the for-await loop prevents a near-deadline timer from firing during reconnect backoff and stamping `"watchdog"` on a recoverable error path. The justification comment is the right one.
- `cancel()` clears watchdog + aborts active controller before any `reconnect()` re-entry can fire.
- `resetCounters()` at the start of each `connect()` attempt → `sse_watchdog_fired` reports per-attempt state, not cumulative lifetime state. Correct semantics for the L2/L3 decision.

**`import type` circular handling**
- `stream-watchdog.ts` uses `import type { ChatStreamReconnectCause } from "@/lib/streaming/stream-transport"` — erased at compile time, no runtime cycle. CONVENTIONS.md update documents this as an explicit exception to the no-circular-dependencies rule with the TS docs link. AGENTS.md "Common pitfalls" mirrors it. Right pattern, right docs surface.
- The transitional `stream-transport-types.ts` from commit 1 (`5a56d4fbf8`) was correctly reverted in commit 2 (`0de0c67761`) once the simpler pattern was confirmed. The reverted file shows up in history but not in the merged diff — net zero new files in `lib/streaming/` besides the watchdog itself.

**Type colocation cleanup (the real bonus)**
- `publish-types.ts` deletion is the most honest fix in this PR: 4 zero-consumer type aliases were dead exports, and `isCredentialError` was a *runtime function* misplaced in `types/`. Moved inline to `deploy-store.ts` where the sole consumer lives.
- `subagent-types.ts` collapses into `fetch-subagent-detail.ts`; docstring explaining the `z.unknown()` schema → SDK type erasure preserved in the owning module. Correct.
- CONVENTIONS.md row tightened: `types/` is for cross-domain shared types with no clear owning module. Types produced by a module live with the producer; consumers use `import type`. This is the rule that should have prevented `publish-types.ts` ever existing — good to lock it in.

**Test relocation accounting**
- 12 tests removed from `stream-transport.test.ts`, 4 relocated to `turn-store.test.ts` → 8 duplicates dropped. Matches PR body. Spot-checked the 4 relocated cases (`SSE completes before poll`, `poll completes before SSE`, `TOOL_USE_START re-activates idle`, `POLL_RECONCILED → stale delta → new send`) — all test `turnReducer` behavior, not transport. Correct destination.
- Watchdog coverage stays in `stream-transport.test.ts` as integration through `subscribeChatEvents` — 102 watchdog/idleTimeout references including the idle-stall reconnect test, the slow-onReconnect-doesn't-trip-watchdog test, and the `sse_watchdog_fired` diagnostic + Sentry breadcrumb assertions. Integration-level coverage is the right call here per audit row #10.

**Reconnect-not-extracted call**
- 15 lines, 5+ closure references (`cancelled`, `reconnectCount`, `connect()`, controller refs). Extracting would require parameter threading that buys nothing. Correct decision to leave inline. The PR resisted the ticket's prescriptive split — that's the right judgement.

**Non-blocking observations**

1. **`conversations.test.ts` `as RawConversationSummary` cast** (commit `238b1bf1bc`) unblocks CI but is the wrong shape of fix long-term. The truthful fix is one line — add `isProcessing: false` to `makeRaw()` defaults. The cast permanently disables the type-safety net for this fixture, so the *next* new required field on `RawConversationSummary` will silently default to `undefined` and the same upstream-merge-time breakage will recur, only this time tsc won't catch it locally either. Fine to land as-is (test helper, sensible defaults intent), but worth a follow-up to swap the cast for an explicit default. Not a blocker.

2. **No dedicated `stream-watchdog.test.ts`**. PR body's audit row #10 explicitly chose integration-through-`subscribeChatEvents` over factory-internal unit tests, and the coverage in `stream-transport.test.ts` is comprehensive. Reasonable. Flagging only because if the watchdog grows complexity (multi-instance, abort-cause threading edge cases, per-attempt-vs-lifetime counter logic), direct factory unit tests are cheaper than integration coverage. Not now.

3. **Defensive double-arm in for-await + `onSseEvent`** — every data chunk arms the watchdog twice (once in SDK callback, once in for-await). The comment justifies it as independence from SDK callback ordering. `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` in V8 are cheap so the cost is negligible; just noting it.

Merge gate: CI 7/7 green at HEAD. Devin "No Issues Found" at `21458c93ce` (early commit — predates 3 follow-up commits including the type-colocation pass and the upstream-merge fixup); worth `@codex review` + `@devin-ai review this PR` at HEAD to formalize closure on the 3 newer commits before merge. The PR body mentions "4 additional findings in Devin Review surface" — worth a 30-second look at app.devin.ai/review/.../pull/32646 before merging.

**Carry-forward**: the meta-pattern of letting `import type` (compile-time only) handle parent-↔-sub-module type sharing instead of inventing a `*-types.ts` companion file is the right default for the codebase. The `publish-types.ts` situation (runtime function misplaced into `types/` to satisfy an org rule) is the failure mode this PR's CONVENTIONS.md tightening prevents.

## Approve — PR C of the LUM-2042 chain, clean migration of 5 storage files to the typed-storage factory

7/7 CI green. Boss-authored via Devin. Two commits: `574bf38661` (migration) → `9b79810717` (audit fixes).

### What I verified

**Factory adoption** (6/6 accessors, correct factory per shape):
- `app-pin-storage.ts` → `createStorageAccessor<PinnedAppEntry[]>` (static key, needs snapshot caching for `useValue`)
- `last-viewed-conversation-storage.ts` → `createKeyedStorageAccessor<string | null>` (per-assistant, imperative-only consumers)
- `context-window-storage.ts` → `createRecordStorageAccessor<ContextWindowUsage>` (Map-like, `maxEntries: 200`)
- `dismissed-surfaces-storage.ts` → `createRecordStorageAccessor<string[]>` (Map-like, `maxEntries: 200`)
- `sidebar-group-collapse-storage.ts` → 2× `createKeyedStorageAccessor<string[]>` (separate keys per Radix root — correct, would have been a regression to share)

**Behavioral equivalence — line-by-line diff against parent (`6f961ed1`):**
- SSR guards: old `typeof window === "undefined"` checks → factory's `readRaw`. ✓
- Empty-string handling on `last-viewed-conversation`: old `raw && raw.length > 0 ? raw : null` → new `parse: (raw) => (raw.length > 0 ? raw : null), fallback: null`. Equivalent (factory short-circuits on `raw === null`). ✓
- `MAX_IDS_PER_CONVERSATION = 500` cap on dismissed-surfaces preserved at call site (factory `maxEntries: 200` is record-level, the 500 is entry-level — two-level cap correctly retained). ✓
- `loadOpenCategories` stale-key filter via `OPEN_CATEGORY_KEYS` set preserved. ✓
- `context-window` `maxEntries` trim — numeric-key caveat in factory docstring N/A here (conversation IDs are UUIDs). ✓

**`pinApp()` mutation fix — real bug caught.** Old: `entries.push(...)` mutated the cached fallback array `[]` shared across `loadPinnedApps()` calls. Latent before (each call returned a fresh `JSON.parse` array), **observable now** because the static accessor snapshot-caches the parsed value to keep `useSyncExternalStore` references stable. Spread (`[...entries, newEntry]`) is the right fix. PR body calls it out correctly.

**Cleanup coverage:** all 6 keys are `vellum:*` prefixed → handled by #32621's prefix sweep in `session-cleanup.ts`. No allowlist additions needed. ✓

**Tests:** 59 tests, all green. `installMemoryStorage` helper adopted by all 3 consumer test files (sidebar/app-pin/last-viewed), eliminating 3× duplicated `MemoryStorage` class + window mocking boilerplate. `afterAll` correctly restores via captured `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`.

### Bot findings — closed

**Codex P2** at `574bf38661` on `sanitize-display-messages.ts:DEFAULT_TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_SEC` (inlined `= 120` would drift from canonical API contract). → Devin reverted in `9b79810717`: inline const deleted, canonical `import { DEFAULT_TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_SEC } from "@vellumai/assistant-api"` restored (the inline was only present because Devin's local generated package was stale; `bun run postinstall` resolved it). Closed at HEAD. ✓

**Devin Review surface** flagged 1 inline issue (same as Codex above — also closed) + "3 additional findings" not visible via REST API. PR body's 20-point audit checklist passes. A 30-second look at https://app.devin.ai/review/vellum-ai/vellum-assistant/pull/32645 before merge would close the gate on those 3 cleanly.

### Non-blocking observations

1. **`createKeyedStorageAccessor` has no `useValue` hook** by design (factory docstring: "compose with `useSyncExternalStore` at the call site"). Both consumers here use imperative `load/save` only, so fine. Worth bookmarking: the next per-entity consumer wanting reactive subscription will need `createRecordStorageAccessor` even if not record-shaped, or the factory gains a keyed `useValue`.
2. **`saveLastViewedConversationId` can't clear** — public API doesn't expose `storage.remove(assistantId)`, so once set there's no way to null via the module's public functions. Probably fine (callers overwrite), but worth a follow-up `clearLastViewedConversationId` export if a callsite needs it.
3. **`createRecordStorageAccessor.load` returns `{ ...fallback }` (fresh object each call), no snapshot caching.** Means it's not safe for `useSyncExternalStore` consumers without external memoization. Currently fine (both record consumers wrap in `new Map` / `new Set` imperatively). If a reactive record-shaped consumer arrives, factory will need the same snapshot-cache treatment as `createStorageAccessor`.

### Carry-forward (procedure)

**Snapshot caching changes the rules for callers.** Once a factory caches parsed values for reference stability, any caller that previously mutated a `loadFoo()` return value becomes a live bug. The `pinApp` fix is the model: when migrating to a snapshot-caching accessor, audit every `load*().push/splice/sort/assign` for in-place mutation and rewrite as spread/non-mutating. Old code's tests still pass; the leak surfaces only at runtime when the cached reference is reused. Filing in pr-review-practices.

- 4 decorators (retry, ratelimit, usage-tracking, call-site-routing) all pass `options` through via spread or direct forward. Verified via diff: `retry.ts -5`, `ratelimit.ts -9`, `usage-tracking.ts -9`, `call-site-routing.ts -9` are all dead-positional-param removals, no logic change.
- 5 concrete providers (Anthropic, OpenAI chat, OpenAI responses, Gemini, OpenRouter) collapse `(messages, tools?, systemPrompt?, options?)` → `(messages, options?)`. Bodies unchanged — values now arrive via `options?.tools` / `options?.systemPrompt` instead of positional binding.
- Plugin pipeline terminal handler in `loop.ts:724` builds `LLMCallArgs` with `tools`/`systemPrompt` inside `options`, then `args.provider.sendMessage(args.messages, args.options)` at `loop.ts:827`. Path is byte-equivalent.
- `LLMCallArgs` (`plugins/types.ts:155`) drops top-level `tools` + `systemPrompt`; JSDoc rewritten to describe `options` carrying the full bag including tools/systemPrompt. Internally consistent with the terminal handler.

**Bot findings**

1. **Codex P2 on `loop.ts:729` (plugin contract break)** — Devin's defense is substantively correct: no internal middleware reads `args.tools`/`args.systemPrompt` directly. I traced every `args.tools` / `args.systemPrompt` reference in `assistant/src/`:
   - `context/compactor.ts:699-700`, `:1069-1070` — `args` here is the compactor's own `CompactionArgs`-style type, NOT `LLMCallArgs`. Compactor reads its OWN fields, then passes them as part of `sendMessage(messages, { tools: args.tools, systemPrompt: args.systemPrompt, signal, config })` to the provider. No coupling to `LLMCallArgs.tools`.
   - `plugins/defaults/overflow-reduce.ts:82` — `args.systemPrompt` from `OverflowReduceArgs`, different type.
   - `plugins/defaults/token-estimate.ts:44` — `args.tools` from `EstimateArgs`, different type.
   - `examples/plugins/echo/register.ts:154` — uses `makeObserver<LLMCallArgs, LLMCallResult>` (observer; doesn't read fields). Type-safe through inference; TS would flag any field reads.
   
   The published `@vellumai/plugin-api` package does NOT yet export `LLMCallArgs` (per the docstring at `plugin-api/index.ts:33`: "Pipeline-argument types (`LLMCallArgs`, `MemoryArgs`, etc.) currently live in `assistant/src/plugins/types.ts` and have not yet migrated into this package"). External plugins cannot be depending on `LLMCallArgs.tools` because the type isn't part of the public surface yet. The change is internal-only at the type contract layer. **Codex is dismissed correctly.**

2. **Devin BUG_0001 on `ratelimit.test.ts:122-125` (half-migrated assertions)** — verified Fixed in `5257fac034`. New assertions correctly read `receivedArgs[1]` as the merged options object and check `.tools` / `.systemPrompt` / `.config` are all present inside it. Real bug, cleanly closed.

**Non-blocking observation worth filing**

**`assistant/docs/plugins.md:386` is now stale.** The pipeline table summary entry still reads:

> | `llmCall` | Every call to `Provider.sendMessage`. Input carries `messages`, `tools`, `systemPrompt`, `options`. |

After this PR, the input carries `messages` + `options` (with `tools`/`systemPrompt` inside options). The prose examples downstream (`Transform input` at L309, `Transform output` at L327, `Short-circuit` at L344) already use `args.options` correctly, so they're aligned with the new shape. Only the table summary needs the one-line edit: `Input carries `messages`, `options` (with `tools`, `systemPrompt`, `config`, `onEvent`, `signal` inside).` — or similar. This is the doc Codex would have actually been right to flag, just for a different reason than the one it offered.

Neither bot caught the doc gap. The right way to think about Codex's finding: the **plugin contract** did change (the type shape that plugin authors will eventually consume once `LLMCallArgs` migrates to `@vellumai/plugin-api`), and the doc that describes that contract is out of sync. The contract change is fine because the package surface doesn't expose it yet; the doc just needs to lead the migration rather than lag it. One-line follow-up; not a blocker.

**Other notes**

- PR body's reflection: `mock.module` bypasses TS, so signature changes need manual mock audit. This PR found 8 stale mocks; #32624 found similar. The repeated finding suggests it's now worth a CI grep — search test bodies for `mock.module(".../providers/...")` and assert that mock signatures match the production type. Tracked in LUM-2058 per PR body, which is the right resolution.
- 282 targeted tests / 767 assertions per PR body — sampled `anthropic-provider.test.ts` (+79/-55), `openai-provider.test.ts` (+66/-70), `openai-responses-provider.test.ts` (+21/-77). All three show direct call-site rewrites destructuring from options or asserting `receivedOptions.tools` — same pattern as the ratelimit fix. Looks systematic.
- Devin Review surface mentions 4 additional findings — worth a 30-second look at app.devin.ai/review/.../pull/32644 before merge.

**Merge gate**: Codex's review is at `c1fb3fc331` (initial), Devin's last response is at `5257fac` (closed BUG_0001) + `37c5f31a` (closed Codex P2). The `37c5f31a32` head is the merge with main + the two earlier substantive commits. Fresh `@codex review` at HEAD would formalize closure of the dismissed P2; Devin's BUG_0001 closure stands.

**Carry-forward**: When a refactor moves fields from a type's top level into a nested `options` bag, the type-level change passes tsc, but `*.md` docs describing the type as a flat list of fields silently drift. Add doc-table audits to the refactor checklist for any `tools` / `systemPrompt` / similar field migration — grep for the field names in `docs/**/*.md` before declaring the refactor complete.

payload.author: vex-assistant-bot
payload.body:
Reviewed HEAD `0c3af1b42d` (post-merge with main, which now contains #32645/#32646/#32630/#32644/#32649). CI green: `Lint, Type Check & Build`, `Type Check`, `Build`, `Test`, `Lint` all success. Architecturally clean. The three Zustand seams (`selection-store`, `lifecycle-store`, `use-active-assistant-id`) carve the data shape the outlet-context plumbing was incidentally bundling.

**Architecture verification**
- **`selection-store.ts`** (47 lines): one field (`activeAssistantId`), one writer (`setActiveAssistantId`), `createSelectors` auto-generates the atomic accessor. Matches the codebase's Zustand v5 pattern.
- **`lifecycle-store.ts`** (89 lines): holds `assistantState` + the trio of imperative actions (`checkAssistant`/`retryAssistant`/`hatchVersion`), with NOOP defaults until `registerImperativeActions` populates them on hook mount. The NOOP defaults eliminate the `?.()` / `!` noise at every call site — fair trade vs. nullable types since the registration race window doesn't manifest in practice (`useAssistantLifecycle` is called first in `RootLayout`, its effects run before child-route effects in the same commit cycle).
- **`use-active-assistant-id.ts`** (29 lines): turns the runtime invariant of `ActiveAssistantGate` into a type-level guarantee (`string`, not `string | null`). The thrown error on gateway bypass is the right kind of loud failure — it surfaces a routing bug as a stacktrace, not a silent null deref.
- **`ActiveAssistantGate`**: reads both stores via atomic selectors, gates on `assistantId && assistantState.kind === "active"`. The placeholder is real loading UX (`Loader2` + "Connecting to your assistant…"), not a `null` return.
- **`RootLayout`**: drives `useAssistantLifecycle` first, then `useAssistantSelectionStore.use.activeAssistantId()` + lifecycle reads, then feeds the sync hooks (`useAssistantFeatureFlagSync`, `useAssistantResourceSync`, `useConversationSync`, `useFeatureFlagBusSync`, `useNotificationIntentSync`, `useEventBusInit`). Hook order makes the logout-clear effect run before the sync hooks' effects in the same commit cycle.
- **Outlet context narrowing**: `ChatLayout` now publishes only the three header-slot setters via `ChatLayoutContextValue` (3 fields). The 8-field `AssistantContextValue` is gone. The retained outlet context is the right tool for the job — header slots hold `ReactNode` with closures, and bundled re-render is the correct semantic there (PR body's justification stands).
- **`assistant-context.ts` deleted** ✓ (verified file absent). The two-layer re-publish (`useRootOutletContext` → `AssistantContextValue` → narrowing in `ActiveAssistantGate`) collapses to one Zustand read.

**Bot findings — all closed at HEAD**

1. **Codex P1 on `selection-store.ts:41` (clear stale on logout)** — closed in `use-lifecycle.ts:574-590`:
   ```ts
   if (!isLoggedIn || isLoading) {
     if (useAssistantSelectionStore.getState().activeAssistantId !== null) {
       setAssistantId(null);
     }
     if (useAssistantLifecycleStore.getState().assistantState.kind !== "loading") {
       setAssistantState({ kind: "loading" });
     }
     return;
   }
   ```
   Guarded reads prevent spurious subscriber wake-ups when already at defaults — the exact optimization PR body mentions. Codex's re-review appears to have missed this clearing logic (which lives in `use-lifecycle.ts`, not in `selection-store.ts` itself). The fix is in place. Worth a `@codex review` ping at HEAD to formalize closure.

2. **Devin BUG_0001 on `chat-page.tsx:166` (AGENTS.md stale)** — closed in `3983a66c26` ("AGENTS.md: outlet context is for layout slots, not app state"). Diff verified: L42 now reads "the side-effect orchestrator `useAssistantLifecycle` runs once in `RootLayout` and publishes everything through Zustand stores under `src/assistant/`" with the three-bullet selector breakdown. The stale `useAssistantContext()` instruction is gone. Devin's review may have been processed before this commit landed; same `@codex review` / `@devin-ai review this PR` ping at HEAD would close it.

3. **Devin ANALYSIS_0001 on `document-viewer-page.tsx:76` (assistantId missing from deps)** — closed in `9b392288d9` ("Fix cold-nav race"). Diff: `[surfaceId]` → `[surfaceId, assistantId]`, AND the page now treats null assistantId as "still resolving" (early return) instead of setting `"No assistant loaded."` error. The cold-nav race Devin was worried about is fixed structurally, not patched. Good shape.

**Non-blocking observations**

1. **Logout race window is one-render, not zero.** When `isLoggedIn` flips to `false`, `useAssistantLifecycle`'s effect runs `setAssistantId(null)` at commit phase. Sibling sync hooks in `RootLayout` (`useAssistantResourceSync`, `useConversationSync`, etc.) run their effects later in the same commit cycle and re-render with `assistantId = null` on the NEXT render — there's a one-render window where they could observe the old id. In practice the auth token is already cleared (that's why `isLoggedIn` flipped), so any fetch against the stale id 401s and dies. The proper fix would be to clear the stores synchronously in the logout call site itself (before `isLoggedIn` flips) — could be a follow-up if you see flake. Not a blocker.

2. **`assistantState` is a discriminated union with object identity per `setAssistantState(...)` call.** Consumers reading via `useAssistantLifecycleStore.use.assistantState()` re-render when the object identity changes, not just when `.kind` does. For consumers that only read `.kind` (a lot of them — `ChatLayout`, `RootLayout`, `ActiveAssistantGate`, multiple sync hooks), this is fine because every transition does change the object. But if you ever add a non-kind field that updates more frequently (e.g. a progress counter or error sub-state), consumers reading only `.kind` would re-render on every progress tick. Worth a thought if the discriminated union grows — split `.kind` into its own store slot, or expose a `useAssistantStateKind()` selector. Not now.

3. **NOOP defaults for imperative actions.** A child route that calls `checkAssistant()` from a *mount* effect (rare in this codebase — current consumers are all event handlers or post-mount paths) would silently no-op on initial mount because effects run bottom-up and RootLayout's `registerImperativeActions` hasn't fired yet. PR body addresses this as a non-issue in practice, which is correct for current consumers. Worth a thought if a new consumer type appears.

**The two LUM tickets that landed differently than originally framed**
- **LUM-2038** (delete `useAssistantLifecycle`) → didn't delete. PR body's justification is right: the hook owns retry budgets, generation counter, stuck-init watchdog, gateway-auth short-circuit, post-hatch cache seed, onboarding-redirect coordination. None collapse onto a query. The correct cut was "delete the outlet-context plumbing," and that shipped.
- **LUM-2037** (move `autoGreetRef` to send-message domain) → discovered dead code. The two `autoGreetRef.current = true` calls in the hook flipped a ref nobody read. Removed; real bug (new auto-hatched signups never get an auto-greet) filed as LUM-2060. Good triage.

**Architectural carry-forward**
The `hook-as-side-effect + Zustand-as-state` pattern documented in `STATE_MANAGEMENT.md:282-292` is the right shape for any side-effect orchestrator that needs to publish to the whole tree. Worth applying to the next eligible target — likely `useEventBusInit` (already partially there) and the various sync hooks if they grow state.

**Merge gate**: CI green at HEAD. All three bot findings substantively closed but Codex's last pass (`3983a66c26`) flagged the now-fixed logout-clear concern — fresh `@codex review` + `@devin-ai review this PR` at HEAD would formalize closure. Devin Review surface mentions 3 additional findings — worth a 30-second look at app.devin.ai/review/.../pull/32641 before merge.

payload.author: vex-assistant-bot
payload.body:
Re-reviewed HEAD `fea1bf0958` (4 commits since my prior APPROVE at `0c3af1b42d`). CI 7/7 green.

**One real Codex P1 worth a one-line fix before merge** — flagging at the top because it's a genuine cold-mount race introduced by `a223a8ddff`, not closed by the subsequent fixes.

---

### Real finding: duplicate `hatchAssistant()` POST on cold onboarding mount

Anchor: `hatching-screen.tsx:120` (the selector subscription) + the hatch effect at L155 with `checkAssistant` in deps L418.

**Trace:**
1. Cold mount of `/assistant/onboarding/hatching`. `RootLayout` calls `useAssistantLifecycle()` which registers callbacks in a **passive** `useEffect` (`use-lifecycle.ts:673-675`).
2. Render 1: `HatchingScreen` reads `useAssistantLifecycleStore.use.checkAssistant()` → captures `NOOP_CHECK` default (registration hasn't committed yet).
3. Commit phase: `HatchingScreen`'s hatch effect runs → `void startHatch()` → cloud path fires `hatchAssistant()` POST.
4. `RootLayout`'s registration effect commits → store updates.
5. Zustand selector subscribers (including `HatchingScreen`) re-render.
6. New `checkAssistant` reference. Effect dep flip → cleanup sets `cancelled = true` (good), new effect re-runs → **second** `startHatch()` → **second** `hatchAssistant()` POST.

The **local** hatch path has `localHatchPromise` module-level dedup (lines 47-49 comment explicitly calls out the HMR/StrictMode case). The **cloud** path has no equivalent guard, so the backend gets two concurrent POSTs from a single user's first launch. This is the highest-traffic onboarding path.

**Suggested fix (single-line):** drop the selector subscription, drop `checkAssistant` from effect deps, and dereference inside `handleHatchReady`:

```ts
// L120 — remove
- const checkAssistant = useAssistantLifecycleStore.use.checkAssistant();

// L201 (inside the setTimeout callback)
- await checkAssistant();
+ await useAssistantLifecycleStore.getState().checkAssistant();

// L418 — drop from deps
```

`handleHatchReady` invokes `checkAssistant` 800ms after the timer fires, by which point registration is guaranteed complete. Reading via `getState()` at the call site is exactly Codex's option (b) — and it's the right one here because the selector subscription is what causes the duplicate-hatch dep flip.

This is the kind of finding worth one more commit before merge. Not blocking architecturally; the structural shape is right.

---

### Other Codex P1s — all closed at HEAD

1. **Selection store logout reset (`selection-store.ts:41`)** — CLOSED in `use-lifecycle.ts:583-590`. Guarded reset on `!isLoggedIn || isLoading` clears `useAssistantSelectionStore` (and `useAssistantLifecycleStore`) to defaults before next session. Codex's REST anchor on `selection-store.ts` is misleading — the reset lives in the lifecycle hook, not the store. Exactly the carry-forward I filed against this PR on the prior pass.

2. **Republish chat-layout context through gate (`active-assistant-gate.tsx:41`)** — CLOSED **structurally** in `54b014fec1` ("Move header slots to Zustand, fix gate-drops-context bug"). Header slots no longer travel via outlet context at all — `useChatLayoutSlotsStore` is the channel. Gated routes register content via store writes from their own effects; the intermediate `<Outlet />` in the gate can't drop what isn't on the outlet. ChatLayout's docstring (`chat-layout.tsx:144`) and AGENTS.md L19 ("Don't ship cross-route state through outlet context") codify the rule.

3. **Hatching screen: subscribe vs render-time getState (Codex P1 on `54b014fec1`)** — CLOSED in `a223a8ddff` ("Subscribe to lifecycle actions instead of capturing them at render"). Line 120 confirms the selector subscription pattern. **But this fix introduced the new race in #1 above.**

### Devin findings

- **ANALYSIS_0001** (`document-viewer-page.tsx:76` — `assistantId` missing from useEffect deps): Devin explicitly acknowledges pre-existing — same behavior held when the read came from `useAssistantContext()`. Out of scope here; worth a one-line follow-up but not blocking.
- **BUG_0001** (AGENTS.md not updated): WRONG. The diff at this PR shows AGENTS.md L41-42 was **rewritten** (selection-store + lifecycle-store description), AGENTS.md L19 added the outlet-context anti-pattern rule, AGENTS.md L20 added the type-colocation + `import type` rule. Devin's anchor is reading against an older AGENTS.md state. Dismiss.

### Architectural verification at HEAD

The two-store split + DI shape is exactly the right cut for this surface:

- **`selection-store.ts`** (47 lines): single `activeAssistantId` field + one writer. Atomic selector subscribers (`useAssistantSelectionStore.use.activeAssistantId()`) only re-render when the id flips, not on every lifecycle phase tick. Note in docstring "If routes ever encode `:assistantId` as a path segment, this store collapses to a `useParams` read" is the right forward marker — this isn't permanent infrastructure, it's the right shape until routes can carry the id natively.
- **`lifecycle-store.ts`** (101 lines): discriminated `AssistantState` + three imperative actions + `registerImperativeActions` writer. Docstring explicitly calls out the no-op-default → late-registration window and **mandates the selector pattern over `.getState()` at render time** — "The store ships no-op defaults that `useAssistantLifecycle` overwrites in a passive `useEffect` after its first render… Subscribing via `useAssistantLifecycleStore.use.checkAssistant()` causes a single additional render when registration lands." The hatching-screen finding is precisely what makes this rule load-bearing — and why the rule needs a companion clause: *callbacks invoked outside the initial commit (timers, event handlers) should `getState()` at call time, not subscribe.*
- **`use-active-assistant-id.ts`** (29 lines): throws if called outside the gate. Right shape — runtime guarantee becomes type guarantee.
- **`use-lifecycle.ts`** (single owner of all writes): retains the polling state machine, recovery timers, generation counter, retry budgets, mutation calls. All the prior `useAssistantContext` consumers now read via stores. LUM-2037's `autoGreetRef` dead-code finding was correctly filed as LUM-2060 instead of being deleted in this PR (right call — out of scope).
- **`active-assistant-gate.tsx`** (74 lines): still passes the `AssistantContextValue` through via `<Outlet context={activeCtx} />`, narrowed for `useActiveAssistantContext()`. Worth noting AGENTS.md says "Inside the gate, call `useActiveAssistantId()`" but the gate still threads a context for legacy `useActiveAssistantContext()` callers. Two side-by-side patterns is fine during the migration; worth a follow-up to collapse on the store-only shape once consumers are migrated.

### `chat-layout.tsx` header-slots Zustand pattern

The `useChatLayoutSlotsStore` shape (chat-layout reads `topBarCenter`, `topBarRightSlot`, `onSearchClick` via selectors; child routes write to it from their own effects) is the right cut. Gated routes (`/assistant/home`, identity, library, etc.) can register header content without the lost-Provider problem. **Note:** module-level singleton — child routes must clear their slot writes on unmount, or stale slot content survives navigation. Worth a quick grep to confirm every writer pairs with a cleanup in its effect's return; non-blocking if Boss has tests covering it.

✦ **APPROVE** at `9d43d4f466` — 7/7 CI green, single commit, 11 files +920/-709.

**Value.** `event-parser.ts` becomes a 351-line routing table from an 863-line monolith with a 640-line switch. Every future event-shape ticket now opens the right ~150-line sub-module instead of scrolling through unrelated cases looking for the one that matters. The orchestrator stays the contract (envelope unwrap → canonical `AssistantEventSchema` → legacy switch); the sub-modules are pure relocation. Zero new behavior, full test coverage preserved.

**Equivalence verified at HEAD**

- **Case coverage matches 1:1.** 28 cases in main → 28 cases at HEAD (22 delegated to sub-modules + 6 kept inline). The only diffs the case-list comparison produced were `{` vs no-`{` (old cases had inline brace-blocks; new delegating cases are one-line `return parse*(data)`). No case dropped, no case added. The diff is a literal rewriting of the same dispatch table into named function calls.
- **Three spot-checked parser bodies are behavior-equivalent.** `parseSecretRequest` is byte-for-byte identical field order and coercion. `parseToolProgress` collapses three local consts (`toolName`/`elapsedSec`/`timeoutSec`) into inline expressions in the return object — same output for every input. `parseSyncChanged` hardcodes its `rawType` argument to `"sync_changed"` in the `unknownEvent` fallback (vs reading the runtime `rawType` parameter), which is correct because `sync_changed` is the only caller of that branch — the runtime value is always exactly that string at the call site.
- **Public API surface is unchanged.** Only `parseAssistantEvent` is exported from `event-parser.ts`. Sub-parsers are internal — consumed only by the orchestrator's switch.
- **`toDisplayAttachments` moved cleanly.** JSDoc preserved verbatim from the old file. The single external caller (`stream-message-updaters.ts:14`) gets its import path updated from `@/lib/streaming/event-parser` → `@/utils/display-attachments`. Grep confirms no other importer needed updating.
- **Tests relocated correctly.** `event-parser.test.ts -83` lines = the 5 `toDisplayAttachments` tests + setup, all now in `display-attachments.test.ts +84` lines. `event-parser.test.ts` has zero remaining references to `toDisplayAttachments`. Integration tests for the parser stay on the public `parseAssistantEvent` entry point — exactly the right test surface to preserve through this kind of split.
- **Canonical schema dispatch is unchanged.** `AssistantEventSchema.safeParse(inner)` runs first; legacy fallback only fires on miss. `mergeEnvelopeConversationId` still grafts the envelope conversationId onto inner messages for legacy events.
- **The 6 inline cases are the right ones to keep.** `assistant_activity_state` / `navigate_settings` / `usage_update` / `turn_profile_auto_routed` each have non-trivial local validation that doesn't fit a sub-module's theme; `error` / `conversation_error` are trivial 1-line returns. Splitting them out would have created either a 4-function "miscellaneous events" module (which is the smell) or 4 single-export files (also a smell). Holding the line at 351 lines and keeping these inline is the right call.

**Small non-blocking notes**

- **Stale doc reference.** `src/types/attachment-types.ts:3` says "populated from SSE event data via `toDisplayAttachments` in the streaming domain." After this PR, the function lives in `utils/`, not `lib/streaming/`. The 20-point audit row #19 is green in the PR body, but this one snuck through. The extraction to `parse-helpers.ts` prevents redefinition across the 5 new sub-modules — so the more accurate framing is "would have been duplicated 5x without extraction," not "was duplicated 3x." Doesn't change the right call (extract it); just a phrasing nit for the PR body.

**Value:** The reframe itself is the right call. Pointing at `src/assistant/queries.ts` + `use-lifecycle.ts` as the canonical example lets each load-bearing pattern stay alive next to the call site it actually protects, which is how the LUM-1814 review cycle already ended up documenting them. Future migrations (LUM-2013/2037/2038) read code, not a side-channel that someone has to remember exists.

**Verifications**

- All 5 anchor line numbers in the PR body resolve to the right patterns at HEAD: `:141` mutation ref stability comment block lives directly above the `hatchMutateRef`/`retireMutateRef` capture; `:204` the `setQueryData` post-hatch seed comment; `:237` + `:270` the recoverable-failure and network-error `setTimeout`-wrapped backoff blocks; `:436` + `:484` the `staleTime: 0` imperative re-check inside `checkAssistant` and the retire-and-rehatch decision path; `:598` the kind-gated data-watcher effect. Anyone reading STATE_MANAGEMENT.md → `use-lifecycle.ts` will land at the same patterns the doc names.
- The two comment rewrites are accurate. The "cache subscriber re-enters" → "data-watcher effect below re-enters" fix matches the actual current shape — the LUM-1814 cleanup pass replaced the imperative `queryCache.subscribe(...)` with a `useEffect` on `assistantResult`, so the old phrasing was misleading-but-still-readable. The rewrite names the timeless invariant — *once we know where we landed, the user shouldn't be silently re-routed by a late-arriving query result* — which will read correctly to someone who arrives here in 2027.

The prose enumeration in the new "Canonical migration example" subsection names four of the five patterns (mutation ref stability, `staleTime: 0` imperative re-checks, `setQueryData` post-mutation seeding, `setTimeout` retry backoff). The fifth — `useEffect`-on-query-data instead of a `queryCache.subscribe()` cache subscriber — is the one your commit message lists at `:598`, and it's arguably the highest-leverage of the five for the next migration to study (the cache-subscriber approach was an early misstep on #32590, fixed mid-cycle). payload.author: vex-assistant-bot
payload.body:
✦ **APPROVE** at `1112e1c5f0` — 6/6 CI green, 7 files +820/-115. **Headline.** PR 1 of LUM-1965, but the substance isn't the tray — it's that the audit on the first sketch surfaced an architectural fix that closes both reviewer findings by construction. The first commit (`f953cf9c97`) added the tray as a 4th "make the main window visible" variant on top of the 3 already living in `index.ts`. The second commit (`1112e1c5f0`) extracted `main-window.ts` as the lifecycle owner, collapsed all 4 variants into a single `ensureVisible()` primitive, and the Codex P2 ("focus before dispatch") + Devin ("ALLOW_ACCESSORY_MODE not flipped") findings both close because the new shape makes them impossible to forget. This is the right way for a bot-driven review cycle to land — the second commit isn't a patch on the first, it's the structural change the findings were pointing at.
Full read ### The extraction lands the pattern, not just the file `apps/macos/src/main/` now has four lifecycle-owner modules following the same `installX` + named-export + module-scope-state shape (`about.ts`, `dock.ts`, `settings.ts`, and now `main-window.ts`). Every future window-manipulating ticket — thread pop-outs LUM-1870, deep links LUM-1872, command palette LUM-1867, sleep/wake LUM-1974 — composes from `ensureVisible()` instead of growing `index.ts` by another 20-line branch. The cost of writing the abstraction now is small; the cost of writing it later, after 4 more callers have each invented their own "what does visible mean?" recipe, is much larger. This is the same first-principles framing #32626 and #32622 just applied to a different module. ### `main-window.ts` API is clean - `ensureVisible()` is the only call site that creates a window. `installMainWindow` is just a once-only wrapper that calls it from `whenReady`. `activate`, `second-instance`, and the tray all compose from the same primitive — no opportunity for the "destroyed window + dispatch" race the P2 finding named. - `toggleVisibility()` correctly gates on `isVisibleAndFocused` rather than just `isVisible`. So clicking the tray icon while the main window is showing-but-behind-Slack focuses it instead of hiding it, which is what users expect from menu-bar apps (Things, Linear, etc.). - `current()` is the BrowserWindow escape hatch reserved for `dispatchToFocused` + `before-quit` cleanup. Not used in this PR — pure API surface for the next 1-2 PRs. Same "ship the abstraction first" pattern as #32604. - `installed` boolean guards bootstrap idempotency; `mainWindow === win` check in the `closed` handler avoids the stale-reference race if a previous-window's close event arrives after a new window has been created. ### Reviewer findings closed by construction - **Codex P2 (focus before dispatch).** New `ensureMainWindow` handler on `TrayHandlers`; conversation menu items call it before `dispatchToFocused`. Test `apps/macos/src/main/tray.test.ts:163-167` asserts the count of `ensureMainWindow` calls increments by 2 across New + Current Conversation clicks. Tray menu-bar item now matches Swift's `NSStatusItem` behavior (showMainWindow → dispatch). - **Devin (ALLOW_ACCESSORY_MODE not flipped).** Flag flips to `true`. The previous comment ("Flip to true in the same change that lands the tray") is replaced with one that explains the post-flip UX (signed-out + zero windows → menu-bar-only, tray is the always-available re-entry point) — exactly the contract `dock.ts:52` was holding for the next reviewer. ### Behavior changes are net positives The PR body calls these out, and they're correct: 1. `second-instance` previously called `focusMainWindow()` which no-op'd when the window was destroyed → second-launch could appear to do nothing if the user had closed the window. Now `ensureVisible()` recreates. Real bug, real fix. 2. `activate` previously only acted when `BrowserWindow.getAllWindows().length === 0` → Dock-clicking on the app while it had visible-but-unfocused state did nothing, despite Swift bringing the window forward. Now matches Swift. 3. Accessory-mode transition on signed-out + no-windows. Drops the Dock icon (per LUM-1966 design); the tray remains as the entry point. ### Tray gotchas handled correctly - Template image (`setTemplateImage(true)`, black-on-transparent bitmap, anti-aliased ring) — macOS auto-inverts for dark mode + pressed state. No-asset PR per the build-from-bitmap approach; the comment names the artwork follow-up. - `setIgnoreDoubleClickEvents(true)` — fast single clicks register as two separate `click`s instead of being swallowed as a double-click. - Module-scope `trayInstance` — keeps the JS handle alive so Node's GC doesn't reap the Tray and leave a ghost NSStatusItem. - No `tray.setContextMenu(menu)` — left and right click both opening the same menu would have collapsed the tray's two intentional gestures. `popUpContextMenu` from the `right-click` listener instead, comment explicitly cites the issue. ### `dock.ts` `computePolicy` purification Unannounced but real: `computePolicy` becomes a pure function of `(visibleWindows, signedIn, allowAccessoryMode)`. Test surface is now a 2x2x2 truth table instead of needing to stand up a `BrowserWindow` registry. Side effect: `formatBadge` also picks up `export` for the same reason. Worth keeping for future Electron-main test work. ### Small non-blocking observations 1. **No explicit `tray.destroy()` on `before-quit`.** In production this doesn't matter — the NSStatusItem is released when the process exits. In dev with main-process hot reload (`bun run dev` rebuilds), the old JS reference is GC-eligible but `popUpContextMenu` can sometimes leave a ghost icon for a beat. Worth a one-liner: `app.on("before-quit", () => trayInstance?.destroy())` next to the daemon-stop call. 2. **`devServerUrl()` is called twice per `createWindow`** — once in `loadUrl()` and once in `installSameOriginNavigationGuard`. Each call re-reads `process.env.VELLUM_DEV_URL`. Tiny; could be hoisted to a `const` at the top of `createWindow` so both consumers see the same string. Same staleness — fresh `@devin-ai review this PR` at HEAD would formalize closure. - **CI:** 6/6 green.
*Two-bot review cycle as a model for future reviewers: when the findings point at a structural absence rather than a local bug, the right second commit is the structural change — not the local patch. This PR is that pattern.*
